News.title: Burnham came to power promising radical change – the signs are that it won’t be for the better
News.content:
Growing pains

ONE of Andy Burnham’s key slogans since becoming Prime Minister is “growth in every postcode”.

Whatever that means.



Yesterday’s quarterly GDP figures show there is still a very long way to go.

Despite the promises, growth has basically flat-lined for over two years.



Tax rises have squeezed incomes and businesses, while giant welfare bills have become a massive drag on the economy.

That has left the construction industry in ruins, shattering any hopes that the Government can build the 1.5million new homes it pledged.



More than one million young people are not in work, training or education as a result of Labour’s National Insurance and minimum wage increases.

What do Burnham and his Chancellor John Healey plan to do about either?

The signs are not good.

More taxes ALWAYS mean less growth. Yet Burnham is planning a wealth whack on individuals and property that will drive away entrepreneurs.



Closer ties with the dying EU won’t deliver growth either.

The ongoing Iran War also threatens to blow a huge hole in Healey’s plans at a time when he MUST ramp up defence spending.

The autumn, with no heatwaves or World Cup to boost spending, could see a painful economic slowdown ahead of Healey’s first Budget.

Burnham came to power promising radical change. The signs are that it won’t be for the better.

Hard Labour

YVETTE Cooper finally admits what most of the country may have decided a long time ago: Labour hasn’t been very good at being in government.



Turning on the man who made her Foreign Secretary, Cooper says Sir Keir Starmer’s hands-off style of management meant their first two years in power were wasted.

Certainly, there have been precious few upsides and plenty of disasters. Welfare up, taxes, spending and debt all up, inflation and unemployment both up and defence spending down.

The Chagos Islands giveaway, the endless U-turns. The Peter Mandelson scandal.

The only question is: Will Burnham prove to be any better?

Dawn of the dud

LABOUR truly is the party of the sneering metropolitan elite.



In response to a post on the struggles of the betting industry — which employs thousands and supports dozens of charities — Dawn Butler MP posted: “lol.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Laughing in the faces of ordinary punters who choose to spend hard-earned money on a harmless flutter is typical of a party that has lost all connection to its working-class roots.

Butler’s attitude reflects many within Labour’s ranks for whom the first instinct is always that Nanny Knows Best.

News.title: When Andy Burnham promised Brits growth in every postcode, did he really mean more illegal migrants?
News.content:
ARE you playing your part? Are you doing your fair share? The Prime Minister wants to know.

It turns out that going to work every day to put a roof over your own family’s head isn’t enough any more. And neither is paying thousands in taxes to fund other people’s families, too.



No, according to Andy Burnham, we all need to do more for the country by accepting our “fair share” of illegal migrants into our local neighbourhoods.

Mr Burnham says middle-class families need to “play their part” when it comes to asylum seeker accommodation, instead of leaving the burden to fall on poorer parts of the country.



He told the country this week: “We cannot have a situation where it’s only the poorest communities in the country that receive all of the dispersal of refugees and asylum seekers.

“I do believe all parts of the country need to work to play their part.”

No10 then doubled down, with a staffer insisting that the PM “feels the current system is unfair, and as a point of principle, he wants to see a redress of the distribution.

“He acknowledges that it would cost more money to do it more fairly, but that is what we need to do”.

Sorry, Prime Minister, but we don’t all have to play our part. We never asked for these people to come here and we don’t want them here.

And it’s not a “point of principle” for us all to have to endure the arrival of thousands of undocumented fighting-age men from far-flung places into our local hotels and residential roads to hang around on street corners, take illegal work and sexually harass teenage girls.



What the PM said is wrong on so many levels.

First, Mr Burnham appears to think that better-off people need to follow poor people who have “accepted” these illegal migrants into their areas.

They absolutely have not.

Illegal migrants have been imposed against their very clearly expressed wishes, and often in the face of opposition from local councils, too.

Apparently Mr Devolution doesn’t like local people power when it comes to asylum seeker accommodation.



Or has he somehow managed to miss all the protests outside asylum hotels in Epping, Crowborough, Canary Wharf, Bristol, Liverpool and Manchester, to name but a few?

The PM also assumes that the middle classes aren’t playing their part already when it’s their taxes which foot the bill for the many billions of pounds spent on migrant accommodation.

Many better-off areas are already sharing the burden, including my own local high street, where the only hotel now only houses asylum seekers.

Only 17 local authorities out of 361 have so far been spared the arrival of illegal migrants in their areas, which hardly suggests most Britons have dodged that particular bullet.

When Andy Burnham promised us “growth in every postcode” on his first day in No10, I don’t think most of us thought he meant that sort of growth.



What was most illuminating from Andy Burnham’s comments, however, was his inadvertent admission that having illegal migrants in your area isn’t necessarily a good thing.

Apparently it’s a burden that we all need to share rather than a blessing.

Who would’ve guessed that all these young men paying people smugglers are not in fact fine, upstanding engineers and doctors desperate to pick up litter and help little old ladies across the road to show their gratitude to us for giving them refuge?



And let’s face it, by calling on us all to share the burden, Andy Burnham was also admitting that he can’t and won’t solve the boats crisis. And he’s not even going to bother to pretend that he will.

Fewer than 300 migrants crossed the Channel on dinghies in December 2018 when the boats crisis first emerged.

It was such a big story at the time that then Home Secretary Sajid Javid had to cut short his family’s Christmas holiday to come home to deal with it.

Eight years later, we see 230 migrants arriving on just one boat in one day and the PM decides to hold an emergency Cobra meeting to discuss . . . the weather and whether to ban disposable barbecues.

Perhaps the only answer is for us all to follow in the footsteps of the Oxfordshire village of Piddington, where the 400 local residents have voted to hold a referendum on seceding from the United Kingdom to prevent 1,250 illegal migrant men from being housed just a few hundred yards away in Bicester barracks.



Meanwhile, all the MPs, charity workers, civil servants, human rights lawyers, BBC and Guardian staff who insist every arrival is a desperate refugee deserving of our sympathy can happily take all these young men into their local communities.

Or, better still, into their own homes.

We’ve seen one illegal immigrant landing on Britain’s shores every 14 minutes since Labour came to power two years ago.

And even though numbers have fallen since last year, most of the illegal boat migrant arrivals — largely fighting-age men from countries with alien cultures — are still here years later.

Indeed, some 200,000 illegal migrants have arrived here since 2018.



And we are still paying for most of them to the tune of some £4billion a year.

It’s not only better-off folk who don’t want illegal migrants in their streets. NO ONE wants them.

We don’t want them in four-star hotels or two-star hotels. We don’t want them in flats, barges or former Army barracks. We don’t want them, full stop.

Spreading asylum seekers around a few more postcodes, shuffling them from inner city sink estates to leafy villages, isn’t the solution to this problem.

The solution is to stop allowing more illegal boat arrivals into our country and to detain and deport the ones who are already here.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The one thing Andy Burnham is right about is that the current system is unfair — but it’s unfair to all British people.

The only “point of principle” he should be caring about when it comes to illegal migrants isn’t which postcode they live in but that people who have no right to live in Britain should not be here at all.

News.title: Bizarre moment boar tries to steal food from sunbather’s bag as swine scavenge on beach at Brit hols hotspot
News.content:
THIS is the moment a group of greedy pigs attempt to pillage food from punters at a ritzy beach.

Eye-raising video shows the brazen boar and its piglets snuffling around an unattended bag in front of a stunned audience on the French Riviera.



The hungry family was captured scouting out the beach before something startled them, sending them scuttling before they could rob the beachgoers, in a now-viral clip.

This summer, hordes of the hungry animals have made quite the impression on France’s holiday beaches.



Wild boars are very common across the Côte d’Azur and rural France but as their population grows, human and pig interactions are becoming far more common.

Their stock is currently growing faster than the authorities can control.



In search of food, they are often fed by humans or help themselves directly from garbage cans.

Growing encounters have caused alarm as some fear the animals are losing their fear of humans.



When a wild animals lose their fear of humans – known as habituation – it triggers a destructive cycle of human-wildlife conflict.

This loss of fear typically happens when urban expansion encroaches on their territory, or when humans intentionally or unintentionally provide food via overflowing trash bins, pet bowls, or handouts.

The best known example of this is the urban pigeon – which have learned over generations that people are a reliable source of food rather than a dangerous predator.



In reaction to the viral clip, Liz Webster, a British farming advocate, said: “Wild boar populations are booming across Europe and on the French Riviera they’ve discovered beaches, tourists, restaurants and bins provide easy pickings.

“Nature needs management.

“In densely populated Europe, bringing back boar, wolves, beavers and potentially bears doesn’t mean humans can simply withdraw and let nature take over.

“Wildlife, farming and people have to coexist and that requires active land and population management.”

It comes as a wild boar went on a dramatic rampage across at a Turkish street in May, sending one man flying and two in hospital.



The savage beast is caught on camera tearing through the middle of a Turkish street, running full pelt towards pedestrians.

One man was seen flipping in the air before crashing face-first onto the road as the crazed creature continues on without care.

News.title: Cops seize £15m of cocaine parcels featuring Man City star Erling Haaland after tip-off about flat-bed truck
News.content:
COPS seize £15million of cocaine in parcels featuring the image of Norway and Man City’s Erling Haaland.

They stopped a flat-bed truck after a tip-off and found a false floor containing 370 packages weighing nearly half a ton.



The packages were wrapped in green plastic and all featured the Norwegian striker in a snap taken in the World Cup

A woman identified only as María R was arrested.



The vehicle was stopped on Wednesday on Ecuador’s Pan-American Highway near the border city of Tulcan.

The city is 153 miles north of the capital of Quito and just a few hundred yards from Colombia.

The South American country is where up to 80 per cent of the world’s cocaine is produced.

Cartels often use public figures to identify shipments so drug couriers know who they belong to and who the buyer is.



Pictures of Lionel Messi, Ronaldo and Maradona have also been used.

Ecuadorian police have seized 80 tons of drugs this year — and 215 tons last year.

Ecuador is a logistical hub in the international drug trafficking network with millions of pounds’ worth of cocaine smuggled there from Colombia.



It is then stockpiled and distributed via Central American routes to America and Europe.

News.title: Cruel Putin bombs Ukrainian passenger trains with suicide drones as hundreds of people travel on board – killing two
News.content:
RUSSIA has blitzed two passenger trains with suicide missiles, leaving one child injured and two dead.

Putin’s bombs hammered the pair of locomotives carrying a total of 890 innocent passengers with jet-powered drones within just hours of each other in Ukraine‘s Odessa region.



Startling footage shows a train driver’s cab completely engulfed in flames following the strike that ultimately killed two crew members.

Russian drones pummelled the first locomotive in the Oblast on the morning of August 13.



The victims of the attack were two crew members, the train machinist and his assistant, the CEO of Ukrainian Railways Oleksandr Pertsovskyi confirmed.

It was carrying 340 passengers, 67 of which were children, on the busy Odesa–Dnipro route.



Hours later a second Kremlin drone struck a train carrying 500 passengers.

One child was injured.



No fatalities have been reported.

President Zelensky posted to X: “Today in the Odesa region, the Russians once again destroyed an ordinary passenger train locomotive with a jet-powered drone.

“There were 340 people on the train.



“And whoever was operating that drone certainly could not have been unaware that the target was entirely civilian.

“As of now, unfortunately, we know that the locomotive engineer and his assistant were killed in the strike.

He continued: “There were also strikes overnight in 11 regions – the Russians used more than 130 attack drones.

“Every day, the Russians strike ordinary people’s lives simply for the sake of terror.

“And unfortunately, far from every such attack receives a strong response from the world.



“More air defence support and more pressure on Russia are needed if the world is serious about stopping this war in Europe.

Russia has struck over 200 Ukrainian locomotives this year according to Euromanidan.

Minister of Communities and Territories Development Oleksii Kuleba said: “Russia has chosen out logisitcs to simply deprive us either of logistics to the ports, logistics to Donetsk Oblast, or frontline logistics.”

Ukraine has now sustained roughly as many locomotive losses in the first half of 2026 alone as in the previous 15 months combined.

A recent report by the United Nations revealed civilian deaths in Ukraine hit a record-high in July, the highest since the first months of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine.



The UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission said in a statement on Thursday: “At least 437 civilians were killed and 2,610 injured in Ukraine in July, a 30 percent increase compared with the previous month and a 70 percent increase compared with July 2025.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

It comes as suspected assassin accused of blowing up a former Ukrainian submarine commander was unveiled as a glamourous woman who defected to Vladimir Putin’s regime.

Margarita Reutt, 32, allegedly acted as a covert Ukrainian intelligence operative before planting a bomb inside a rubbish bin and remotely detonating it in Sevastopol.

News.title: Couple’s wedding day saved by bride’s grandad’s mobility scooter after groom breaks leg & ankle in drunken stag do fall
News.content:
A GROOM who broke his leg and ankle on his stag do got married sat in a mobility scooter borrowed from his bride’s grandad.

Andy Sheldon, 47, used it to help him get around with wife Lisa, 42, on their big day.



She sat on his lap as he zipped about on the machine.

And they had a spin on the dance floor while he was on the electric vehicle.



Gym instructor Andy said: “At first I was gutted on my wedding day as I felt I’d let Lisa down.

“I like dancing all night so it was a bit annoying that I couldn’t get up and dance.

“But I took it in my stride even though my foot was throbbing.”

Social worker Lisa said: “One thing I was thinking before the wedding is, ‘If he’s on crutches we won’t be able to hold hands and walk around together’.

“But when he was in his chair we could. That was an absolute godsend.”

Guests loved Andy’s entrance to Ed Sheeran hit Thinking Out Loud, featuring the lyrics, “When your legs don’t work like they used to before.”



Lisa said: “When we did our entrance song, we were meant to walk down this staircase together but we obviously couldn’t do that.

“I walked down the staircase and Andy used the fire exit out the back. I came in to Raye song Where is My Husband!”

Andy broke his left shin, calf bone and ankle falling down train station stairs in Leeds.



The ankle ended up pointing in the wrong direction.

The dad of two needed surgery to pin the bones together.

After he revealed his wedding was in a week, the hospital found a cancellation and rushed his op through.



But he was still left needing to use crutches and a medical boot.

The couple from Hull, who had their big day in nearby Driffield, had to cancel their honeymoon to Italy while he recovers.

They now plan to head to Bali in September.

News.title: How 100s of teens are descending on Brighton to booze & brawl as social media ‘meet-ups’ turn violent for TikTok likes
News.content:
IT’S the trendy seaside town favoured by DJ Fatboy Slim and Housing Secretary Angela Rayner.

But Brighton has been named the teenage boozing capital of Britain, with the highest number of underage drinkers ending up in hospital there.



Residents say the famous esplanade becomes “lawless” on sunny weekends as social media-organised “meet-ups” turn violent.

Youths have been seen taking drugs and necking vodka before fights — intended to win TikTok likes — break out in front of baying spectators, as well as terrified holidaymakers and locals.



Brighton sailing club committee member Angus Malcolm has seen youngsters urinating in the streets and lighting fires next to his boats.

Angus, 51, said: “They turn up en masse, 200 or 300 of them.



“They will pick an area at the last minute, such as the beach, then descend on it.

“There will always be boozing and fighting and drugs.

“The first bank holiday when there was lots of sun, this was not a nice place to be.

“There was loads of aggro, lots of fights and groups of people. It was bad all weekend but certainly in the evening and someone was stabbed.



“That weekend it felt lawless. There is a bit more of a police presence now.”

Recent figures show that the number of alcohol-related under-18 hospital admissions in Brighton and Hove are 170 per cent higher than the national average.

Across almost every UK region, under-18 girls now account for the highest proportion of alcohol-specific hospital admissions.

And 15-year-old girls in England now report higher rates of monthly drinking than boys of the same age.

Mother-of-two Alex Costlin has been shocked at the number of underage girls in skimpy outfits she has spotted boozing in Brighton.



Speaking outside the seaside shop where she works, she said: “It’s quite scary really because they are so fragile and innocent and they all dress the same. They are almost naked.

“I’m not judging but they get so drunk. It’s no wonder they end up in hospital and it’s very sad to see because they are destroying their health.

“They take drugs too. Sometimes they come into the shop asking me for help with their laughing gas balloons. I say no.



“There are riots all the time, fights and everything.”

The riots Alex describes are the result of unofficial parties organised on the internet.

Promoters make claims like “free entry”, provide sound systems and promise that weed and nitrous oxide balloons will be available for sale.

The trade in drugs is no doubt the motive for planning such occasions.

Youngsters are encouraged to bring their own alcohol and volunteers in Brighton complain there has been an explosion in BuzzBallz litter during the summer months.



BuzzBallz are powerful cocktail-like drinks high in alcohol that have become popular with teenagers.

Around 300 tons of rubbish was collected on Brighton beach last year, with campaigners saying the majority was single-use plastics.

The Leave No Trace group found 3,600 crisp packets, lolly wrappers or sandwich containers, 800 aluminium drink cans and 740 plastic bottles in just five beach cleans.

Marcos Montoya, 40, runs an ice cream store close to Brighton pier and he is calling for greater police presence to combat the yobs.

He said: “There were fights as soon as summer started. A big crowd surrounded about four people aged 15 or 16 who were fighting. They were young kids.



“They were making live TikToks and streams and they were doing it for likes. I don’t know how they are managing to buy the alcohol — they always ask for ID here.

“Some of them are so drunk they need help walking.”

Labour MP Angela Rayner — who was slammed for failing to pay the correct stamp duty on the purchase of her flat in Hove — is promising to build more council houses to help seaside towns like Brighton.

But events supervisor Emily McMillan says more needs to be done to improve hospitals in the area.

Emily, 23, said: “A&E in Brighton is an absolute nightmare and it’s clogged with teenagers. I went in for a head injury before and I was kept waiting around for 12 hours.



“There were so many people and some of the teenagers looked like they were under the influence.”

Mother-of-five Jane Griffin, 65, helps run her family clothing store on the seafront.

She feels that teenage boozing is something residents have to put up with, especially as the city is so hedonistic.

Jane said: “I think it’s a shame that Brighton is labelled with that because teenage drinking is widespread. It is a rite of passage.

“They go through a stage of experimenting with drink and drugs, but most come out the other side and I’ve got five successful children. They’re thriving.



“Of course I worried about them, but I think there’s a lot of doom and gloom around teenage years and everyone grows up.

Councillor Bella Sankey, leader of Brighton & Hove City Council, said: “We know people are worried about young people drinking and gathering in large groups, and we are addressing these concerns.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Brighton & Hove is a busy place for visitors, so we’re working closely with police, health services and youth teams to help keep young people safe, carry out checks across all venues, and offer support early.

“Our aim is to stop harm before it happens by giving young people better choices, clear advice and the right help when they need it.”

News.title: Rare reptile which washed up in Anglesey flown back to Gulf of Mexico in epic 5,000-mile trip after two years in rehab
News.content:
A RARE turtle that washed up on our shores is on a 5,000-mile trip home after a two-year rehab.

Rhossi, a critically-endangered Kemp’s ridley sea turtle, was smeared in sex lubricant KY jelly and Vaseline to stop him drying out on the flight.



He safely arrived in Houston, US, after ten hours in the hold — and next Tuesday will be released into the Gulf of Mexico.

Rhossi was “cold-stunned” — ­battling hypothermia — and close to death when found by a dog and its owner in December 2023.



Barely 25cm long and weighing less than 1kg, the tiny turtle was taken from Llydan Beach, near Rhosneigr, to Anglesey Sea Zoo. He has since grown to 21kg (3st, 4lbs) ahead of his trip home.

The zoo’s owner Frankie Hobro said: “We’ve had to slather Rhossi in KY jelly and vaseline to try and stop him from dehydrating — which is always quite an amusing one going to buy that at the chemist!

“But this is the moment we’ve been working towards every single day for more than two years, so it’s incredibly emotional.

“Rhossi arrived with us fighting for life, and now we’re preparing to watch him make the journey home where he belongs.”



So far, Rhossi’s journey has seen him travel via helicopter from Anglesey to Heathrow then by cargo flight to Houston. He will be put in a large tank provided by Houston Zoo then taken south to be released into the warm waters near Texas’s Padre Island.

Frankie added: “We’re doing loads of tests on him now. Blood tests and all the medical stuff like his weight and strength, to make sure he’s good to have a satellite tracker fitted, which we’re hoping will go really smoothly.

“This will take a couple of days to turn around before we head to Padre Island, where we know there is a really healthy breeding population of Kemp’s ridley sea turtles that are at the tail end of their breeding season.



“They’ve managed to re-establish the species there, and we are pretty sure that’s where Rhossi’s originated from as a hatchling.

“It’s wonderful as we’re having all these people there for the release — everyone that has been involved in his transfer from the US. He’s a big lad so I’ll need someone to help me carry him into the sea!”

Rhossi is the fourth cold-stunned sea turtle rescued and rehabilitated by Anglesey Sea Zoo over the past decade, representing three different endangered species. Each turtle was first discovered by a dog.



Conservationists have said juvenile turtles are occasionally carried across the Atlantic by currents before becoming cold-stunned in northern European waters in winter.

The only two remaining nesting beaches for Kemp’s ridley sea ­turtles are in Mexico and Texas.

News.title: Two seriously hurt as passenger train derails in East Sussex
News.content:
Twenty people have been injured, two seriously, after a train derailed in East Sussex and a major incident was declared.

Network Rail said the 14:24 BST Southern service from London Victoria to Eastbourne came off the tracks close to Lewes railway station, shortly before 16:00 BST.

Photographs from the scene showed people standing on top of overturned carriages, with passengers describing "pandemonium" on board and screaming.

British Transport Police said three carriages derailed, leaving several people trapped. All 150 on board have now been evacuated.

Several rail routes in the area were closed, as emergency teams rushed to the scene and people were advised to avoid the area.

Patients were assessed and treated at the scene, with some sent to local hospitals.

British Transport Police Chief Superintendent Dominique Ioannou said in a press briefing on Thursday night that a number of passengers were initially trapped but were all safely evacuated from the train.

She said while two people sustained serious injuries, a further 18 suffered less serious injuries.

"The train started rocking violently and then I remember clocking eyes with this guy and then there was a lot of screaming," passenger Rachel Heath said.

"It felt like we flew in the air and the carriage landed on its side and it slid. I felt like it was going to completely flip over.

"There was a mum who was bleeding from her mouth and a dad and his son who had cuts. It was like a movie."

News.title: UK sees hottest day of the year as 38.1C recorded in Kew Gardens
News.content:
The UK has experienced its hottest day of the year and fifth hottest day on record, as a heatwave that gripped much of the country peaked at 38.1C on Thursday, the Met Office said.

Kew Gardens in west London recorded England's top temperature, provisionally surpassing the 38C recorded in Lingwood, Norfolk on 26 June.

The latest spell of extreme heat marks the UK's fifth heatwave this year, with the Met Office warning this summer is on course to be the UK's hottest since records began.

An amber heat health alert, warning of significant detrimental impacts to health and social care services is in place across the whole of England until 21:00 BST on Friday.

News.title: Five key takeaways from results day 2026
News.content:
Results for A-levels, T-levels, BTecs and other vocational qualifications are out.

And this year, they've come at a time when all eyes are on what teenagers decide to do next.

Universities are keen to get them through the door. As they grapple with their finances, they know that every filled seat in a lecture hall comes with tuition fee funding.

The new prime minister, meanwhile, wants to carve out clear routes into technical jobs that can rival the well-established path of A-levels and a university degree.

For teenagers, considerations about the immediate and long-term cost of university, as well as the availability of other options, are all in the mix.

Here are the standout things you need to know.

News.title: Son of 102-year-old says father died after being 'pushed off stage'
News.content:
Robert said: "He just asked them to turn the music down."

He said his father turned around to come back down off the stage when he was pushed, and that resulted in a broken hip.

"[That's] the most upsetting part. He wasn't going to live forever but it's not a nice way, obviously in pain," he said.

"We want to see justice, of course.

"They must have known he was an old man. It makes you wonder what the world is coming to.

"It has obviously made it difficult. It would've been nice if he'd gone quietly in his sleep.

"He was in hospital, suffering, for a week-and-a-half. It's not nice.

"I feel sad - even though he could be difficult because of his age and dementia, still, you get used to him being around," he said.

Robert, a retired civil engineer, said his father used to visit the Crow's Nest.

"What happened is not nice. The pub has changed a lot over the years. It has become a youngsters' pub," he said.

Robert said he grew up in the home in the the Llanyrafon neighbourhood where his father had lived since 1960.

He said his dad had a career as a design draughtsman and had lived alone since his wife died 40 years ago.

"Me and my brother would visit our father regularly, and clean the house and buy him food.

"His eyesight had deteriorated and he had been diagnosed with dementia two or three years ago."

Robert said: "He's well-known around here, although a lot of his generation are gone," he added.

He said his father would visit the pub two or three times a week, where he would drink beers, and described how he became a familiar face to some locals.

"I suppose he became a pub character," he added.

News.title: Hunt surges to 200m glory to win second European gold
News.content:
Britain's Amy Hunt charged to 200m glory to secure her second gold medal of the European Championships as Dina Asher-Smith settled for bronze in Birmingham.

Hunt, who won 100m gold on Monday, reeled in rival and compatriot Asher-Smith down the back straight to cross the line first in a season's best time of 22.19 seconds.

With the women's and mixed 4x100m relay events left to race, the 24-year-old remains on course to fulfil her goal of "being iconic" to become the first athlete to win four European Championship gold medals in the same tournament.

Ireland's Rhasidat Adeleke set a new national record as she pipped Asher-Smith to silver.

"Two out of four baby," Hunt, 24, told BBC TV.

"This is becoming a magical week and one I will remember for the rest of my life."

After struggling in the 200m earlier this summer, Hunt said she was ready for a "renewal of our vows" in the event.

And the Briton kept her promise with a composed performance that ended with her powering through the final 40m to beat her competitors and clinch gold.

She held her arms aloft and pointed to the sky in celebration after emulating Asher-Smith's 100m-200m European double in 2018.

After getting off to a rapid start, Asher-Smith was unable to hold off Hunt and Adeleke in the final push, but in finishing third she claimed a ninth European medal - a tally only bettered by the 10 of Polish ex-sprinter Irena Szewinska.

"I'm disappointed to have a bronze but I think 10 years after my first medal, it is such an achievement to be in a place to come back year after year," Asher-Smith said.

Before the race, there were hopes of a British one-two-three on the podium, with Asher-Smith, Hunt and Success Eduan holding the three fastest times in Europe times this year.

However, Eduan - who beat Hunt to win her first British title in June - finished sixth.

Hunt's second gold continues Britain's dominance in the sprint events in Birmingham after Romell Glave and Jeremiah Azu secured a one-two finish in the men's 100m, while Matthew Hudson-Smith stormed to 400m victory on Wednesday.

News.title: The key signs you may have damaged your eyes by looking at the eclipse
News.content:
Eye experts are warning people to be on the alert for any signs their vision has been damaged by looking at the sun during Wednesday's eclipse.

The symptoms can include blurred vision, a central blind or dark spot and increased sensitivity to light.

After the previous total eclipse of the sun that was visible in the UK in 1999, around 70 people were left with damaged sight.

Many of them had spent less than a minute looking at the spectacle, without realising they were harming their eyes.

The danger comes because staring at an eclipse without protection can damage the retina, which sits at the back of the eye, and particularly those cells responsible for sharp central vision.

The sun is incredibly bright, even when partially obscured by the moon.

Normally if we stare at it, we wince and quickly look away.

But when it is darker, during an eclipse, that instinct may not kick in, even while our eyes are being damaged.

The bright light and ultraviolet radiation given off by the sun can lead to a condition known as "solar retinopathy".

And because the retina has no pain receptors, it's hard for people to notice the damage as it happens, so symptoms may only appear several hours later.

Leading up to the eclipse itself, experts were warning only genuine specially-designed solar eclipse glasses should be used, and that ordinary sunglasses or other devices were not enough to prevent potential damage.

News.title: BBC Verify speaks to woman who filmed ICE agent pointing gun at her
News.content:
A video showing a US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent pointing his gun at a woman has been viewed by millions after she shared the moment on Instagram.

Carolina Molina says she was out delivering business cards in Falls Church, Virginia, when she saw ICE agents, who then surrounded her car.

The US Department of Homeland Security said she "attempted to harm officers by weaponising her vehicle". Molina denies this.

BBC Verify assesses the dashcam footage shared by Molina. Jake Horton reports.

Produced by Tom Joyner. Graphics by Mark Edwards.

News.title: How to get a good night's sleep during hot weather
News.content:
Hot weather can make you feel tired and lethargic during the day.

That is because you are using more energy to regulate your internal temperature.

But if your sleep is disturbed at night, try to avoid napping during the day.

When it is hot, feeling sleepy can be precious - save it for bedtime.

News.title: Honeytrap thieves jailed for killing men they had drugged
News.content:
A couple who drugged men seeking sexual services in order to steal from them have been jailed for killing two men and poisoning others.

Adina Mihai and Madalin Dumitru admitted the manslaughter of Gary Mouat, 37, from Oxfordshire, and Malcolm King, 80, from Gloucestershire, in 2025 and 2024 respectively.

On the first day of their trial in June, the pair also each admitted two further counts of administering poison to surviving victims.

Mihai, 31, and Dumitru, 30, were both sentenced to 17 years in prison at Oxford Crown Court.

Mihai, who posed as a sex worker, and her partner Dumitru, arranged to meet men paying for services she had advertised online at their homes.

The court heard four had their alcoholic drinks spiked with the powerful sedative gamma-butyrolactone (GBL) so the pair could steal from them.

Two men died as a result, while two others - who cannot be named due to reporting restrictions - survived.

News.title: Big Issue says vendors struggling as sales hit by heatwaves
News.content:
Big Issue vendors are struggling to sell magazines in the UK's extreme heat, which is having an "immediate" impact on their earnings, Big Issue's managing director says.

Sales of the British news and entertainment magazine are down on average 20% year on year in weeks where heatwaves have been declared, Catherine Parsons said.

During June's record-breaking temperatures, the worst-hit West Midlands and Wales saw 34% and 33% fewer sales respectively.

George Anderson, who sells the Big Issue near the BBC's Broadcasting House in London, says it is a struggle when footfall is lower and people would rather be near the aircon.

"People are uncomfortable, they don't want to hang around in the heat and chat," he told the BBC on the hottest day of the year.

"I manage it as best I can, and so far so good, but my sales are definitely down which can be quite tough."

Big Issue is sold by people experiencing homelessness or financial instability.

But Parsons said sellers are losing out on vital income due to the heatwaves.

"For most of us, extreme heat is an inconvenience. For Big Issue vendors, it means earning significantly less and making difficult decisions about rent, food and other essentials," she said.

In the week of 22 June, when the UK's June temperature record was broken and temperatures hit 37.7C (99.9F), Big Issue sales fell by an average of 22% compared to the same week the previous year, their figures show.

The latest spell of extreme heat marks the UK's fifth heatwave this year, with the Met Office warning this summer is on course to be the UK's hottest since records began.

Parsons said Big Issue teams were working to support vendors and had been handing out sunscreen, caps and water bottles.

"But in the most extreme temperatures, it's simply unsafe for vendors to be out and selling, and when the heat forces them to cut their working day short, the financial impact is immediate."

News.title: Dad to stand trial accused of murdering daughter Minnie Merriman
News.content:
The father of a nine-year-old girl who died after being found seriously injured at an industrial estate in Arbroath is to stand trial accused of her murder.

Prosecutors allege Christopher Rice, from Wakefield, West Yorkshire, killed Minnie Merriman, who died in Dundee's Ninewells Hospital on 3 August.

The 35-year-old, who was remanded in custody, made no plea during a second appearance in private via videolink at Forfar Sheriff Court. He was fully committed for trial.

Minnie's family previously paid tribute to their "beloved, absolutely incredible, beautiful and brave Minnie Moo".

Emergency services were called to the Elliot Industrial Estate in Arbroath shortly after midnight on 3 August following reports that a child had been found injured.

Minnie was taken to Ninewells Hospital alongside four other people, but later died as a result of her injuries.

Police Scotland said they were not looking for anyone else in connection with Minnie's death and the other members of the family - who were camping in the area - are being supported by specialist officers.

News.title: Second attempted murder arrest after cycle path attack
News.content:
A second suspect has been arrested on suspicion of attempted murder after a man was attacked on the Bristol to Bath Railway Path.

The victim, aged in his 30s, was taken to hospital with non-life-threatening injuries believed to have been caused by a "bladed weapon" following the incident near Bitton at about 20:00 BST on Tuesday.

One teenager was arrested on the night of the attack and a second was arrested on Wednesday afternoon.

Both have been released on conditional bail while enquiries continue.

Insp Barny Mabbett, from Avon and Somerset Police, said: "Uniformed officers are conducting patrols along the railway path to provide reassurance because we recognise an incident like this does inevitably causes concern.

"Our investigation into what happened is ongoing, but we are also working with other organisations around making sure the railway path is a safe place for people to enjoy and use both in the short-term and long-term."

News.title: Leicester City put up for sale for more than £200m
News.content:
Leicester City are looking to sell the club for more than Â£200m, with its Thai owners King Power ready to leave after 16 years.

The Foxes have had an eight-page sales booklet produced by a leading US investment bank to help offload the one-time Premier League title winners.

Citigroup lists the Foxes, its women's team, and other major assets - including the 32,000-seat King Power Stadium and its Seagrave training facility which was opened in 2020 and is valued at Â£121m - as well as OH Leuven, Leicester's Belgian sister club, as up for sale in a brochure titled 'Project Lineup'.

The document, seen by BBC Sport, values the club's physical assets at more than Â£200m, though no specific sum has been attributed to the sale of its struggling teams.

The brochure speaks of "a rare opportunity to acquire a club with an excellent track record of winning promotions to higher divisions".

Leicester's successes, including the 5,000-1 Premier League title win of 2016 and the FA Cup triumph five years later, are well promoted in the brochure, while their place in League One, after back-to-back relegations from the top flight and the Championship, fail to get a mention.

The club's turnover, which Citigroup forecast to be more than Â£97m for the 2026 financial year are also part of the pitch, but the years of financial losses and the club's debts - which, as outlined in its 2025 accounts, include Â£103.6m in bank loans - are omitted.

In the years that the club yo-yoed between the Premier League and Championship, with two relegations from the top flight in three years between 2023 and 2025, the club lost more than Â£180m.

News.title: Bishop appears in court over child rape charges
News.content:
A 70-year-old bishop has appeared in court for the first time accused of two counts of rape against a female under the age of 16.

David Oakley, the Bishop of Northampton, was charged in June following an investigation by Staffordshire Police.

He appeared at Westminster Magistrates' Court via videolink from his lawyer's office.

Oakley was not asked to enter a plea during the hearing as Chief Magistrate Paul Goldspring sent the case to the Old Bailey.

Oakley was released on bail, with conditions not to contact the alleged victim, or her family, ahead of a plea hearing on 10 September.

The incidents allegedly took place in Staffordshire between February 2000 and February 2001, when Oakley was in his mid-40s working as a Catholic priest.

Oakley was born in Stourbridge, West Midlands, and ordained as a priest in 1980 before becoming Bishop of Northampton in 2020.

Oakley retains the title of Bishop but has withdrawn from public ministry.

The Catholic Diocese of Northampton - which covers Northamptonshire, Bedfordshire and Buckinghamshire â said in a previous statement that it recognised the case was "very distressing for all concerned".

News.title: Human bones found in south-east London garden
News.content:
Human bones found in the garden of a bungalow in south-east London are being examined by the Met Police.

Officers were called to Aperfield Road in Biggin Hill at about 15:30 BST last Friday, the force said.

The bones were sent for specialist examination which confirmed they were human. They are now undergoing further tests to establish their age and identity, police added.

The area around the home was cordoned off for six days, according to The Sun, external, with one resident telling the newspaper the property was being renovated.

"The builders discovered something on Friday and of course they completely had to stop work," they added.

A Metropolitan Police spokesperson added: "The crime scene is now closed and an investigation remains ongoing to establish the full circumstances."

News.title: Ski Sunday host Chemmy Alcott suffers collapsed lung after jumping into lake
News.content:
Ski Sunday presenter Chemmy Alcott says she suffered a collapsed lung after jumping into a lake while on holiday in France.

The 44-year-old former GB Olympic skier posted a clip on Instagram, external that showed her jumping off a five metre platform into Lake Annecy, in the French Alps, before landing badly and ending up in hospital.

"Most people badly time a front flip off a five-metre platform and get winded," she said in the clip.

"I apparently don't do things by halves. Collapsed lung, chest drain and a very expensive lesson in rotation."

Alcott explained that she initially went back to jump again after her difficult landing, out of "embarassment" and "just so I wasn't making a big deal out of it".

But she soon realised she "couldn't breathe properly and should probably go and get it checked out".

She later shared images of herself in hospital with tubes and wires sticking out of her body.

In the caption to the main clip - titled "this didn't end well" - she wrote: "Well... that escalated quickly. Turns out five metres is quite a long way to discover you've got the rotation wrong.

"One badly timed front flip. One very hard landing. One collapsed lung. One chest drain. And a few more hospital overnights than were on the holiday itinerary...

"I absolutely loved Annecyâ¦ but I'm not entirely sure it loved me back."

A collapsed lung - medically known as a pneumothorax - occurs when air becomes trapped in the space between the lung and the chest wall, according the NHS.

CNN host Dana Bash put Republican Rep. Mike Lawler on the hot seat Thursday about why he won’t return campaign donations from Rep. Max Miller despite allegations of spousal and child abuse against the Ohio congressman.

The attacks come as Miller faces a House Ethics Committee investigation into allegations of domestic violence leveled by ex-wife Emily Moreno, the daughter of Ohio Republican Sen. Bernie Moreno. She has also alleged Miller broke the collarbone of their 2-year-old daughter. Miller has vehemently denied the claims and any wrongdoing and insisted he will stay in the race.

During the interview on CNN’s Inside Politics, Bash asked Lawler, who represents New York’s 17th district, about receiving $10,000 from Miller’s PAC. “You have no plans to return the money?” Bash asked Lawler, adding, “Miller has been accused of abusing his ex-wife and his daughter. Why have you decided not to return the $10,000?“

Lawler said that he had spoken to the Ohio congressman, whom he considers a friend, about his divorce and that it was a private matter that should play out in family court. He then tried to pivot the argument to his re-election opponent, Democrat Cait Conley, who has pulled up even in some recent polling against the incumbent, saying that she received donations from disgraced former New York Gov. Eliot Spitzer, who resigned in 2008 when he was implicated in a high-end prostitution ring as the infamous “Client-9.”

But Bash was not having it and brought the conversation back to Miller. “I'm asking you specifically about Max Miller. So, it sounds like you — you said you talk to him a lot privately — it sounds like you’re saying you’re not returning the donations because you believe him.”

open image in gallery CNN's Dana Bash presses NY Rep. Mike Lawler on donations from Ohio Rep. Max Miller Thursday ( CNN )

“Look, this is a private family matter, that has unfortunately has spilled out into the public,” Lawler responded.

“Max has been accused, Max has also made allegations against his ex-wife. It is tragic, and obviously, I don’t condone any level of abuse, but ultimately there’s been nothing that has been corroborated here.”

Bash pressed him further on why he would notjust return the $10,000 he got from Miller’s pac since its small potatoes compared to the $4.8 million he has on hand for his campaign.

“Is it the principle, because its your friend and you believe him?” she asked. “Why not just give it back?”

Lawler insisted there has “been nothing to veriify any of the claims that have been leveled” against Miller.

open image in gallery Rep. Max Miller (R-Ohio) has donated to a slew of Republican incumbents. Some Democrats are hitting their opponents for it. ( Reuters )

In Pennsylvania’s 7th Congressional District, Bob Brooks hit Rep. Ryan Mackenzie for receiving $2,500 from Miller’s committee in March of 2025.

“Ryan Mackenzie is showing his true colors. He took thousands in campaign cash from Max Miller, a congressman facing serious allegations that he violently abused his ex-wife and hurt their young daughter, but Ryan doesn't care,” Brooks spokesman Benny Stanislawski said.

“That's who he is: open for business for whoever's willing to pay up, no questions asked. He's said nothing about whether he'll keep the Miller money. He must apologize and return the money immediately.”

When contacted by The Independent, the Mackenzie campaign focused on Miller and Brooks.

“Congressman Mackenzie takes charges like those against Rep. Max Miller very seriously and, if proven true, the campaign would certainly donate it to a charity to help domestic abuse victims,” Andres Weller, Mackenzie’s campaign manager said in a statement. Weller also pointed to a lawsuit where a judge ruled that Brooks had to pay $162,000 to his former mother-in-law, according to Lehigh Valley Public Media.

“Congressman Mackenzie has repeatedly called on Bob Brooks to repay the $162,000 it has been proven that he stole from his own family and which a judge has ruled he needs to pay. To date, he has chosen to ignore that court order.”

In addition, in Michigan’s 7th district, Democratic nominee Will Lawrence criticized Rep. Tom Barrett on X for receiving $2,500 from Miller’s PAC in March of 2025.

open image in gallery Rep. Ryan Mackenzie (R-PA) has drawn heat for accepting money from Max Miller’s PAC ( Getty )

“This is who Tom Barrett associates with,” Lawrence posted on X. “He claims to be a family man, but he's taken thousands in campaign cash from a man credibly accused of abusing his ex-wife and daughter. Max Miller shouldn’t be in Congress and Tom Barrett should return this money.”

The Independent has contacted the Barrett campaign for comment.

The National Republican Congressional Campaign Committee said Democrats criticizing the campaign contributions given that other Democratic members of Congress who have been accused of sexual misconduct or faced allegations gave money to their colleagues.

“Democrats are shameless hypocrites who conveniently look the other way when their vulnerable members are bankrolled by scandal-plagued Democrats like Eric Swalwell, Ruben Gallego, Jimmy Gomez, and Bobby Pulido,” spokesman Mike Marinella said in a statement. “Nobody should take these slimeballs seriously when their supposed principles disappear the second they become politically inconvenient.”

Rep. Eric Swalwell of California was forced to resign after he faced accusations of sexual misconduct and one woman accused him of rape. Earlier this year, CNN reported that Gomez faces an Ethics Committee investigation relating to sexual misconduct allegations. Texas Democratic candidate Bobby Pulido faces criticism for his ties to a bandmate who was a registered sex offender. And Sen. Ruben Gallego (D-Ariz.) has come under criticism for dating two former congressional staffers.

Democrats also supported Maine Senate nominee Graham Platner for months before they pushed him to exit the race after Politico reported an accusation that he allegedly sexually assaulted an ex-partner.

Both Barrett and Mackenzie won their seats in 2024 in highly-contested races. The Cook Political Report lists both of their contests this November as “Toss Up.” President Donald Trump won both districts.

President Donald Trump has so far publicly stuck with Miller, who worked in his first administration. But other Republicans, including Moreno, have called for his exit from Congress.

open image in gallery Sen. John Husted (R-OH) has called on Miller to drop his reelection bid ( Getty )

Sen. Jon Husted, who also received money from Miller in the past, called on Miller to resign.

“I believe Max would be making the right decision to step aside as a candidate and resign from Congress to focus on what is in the best interest of his daughter,” he said on X. “Years from now, I believe he will look back and know it was the right choice for her.”

Democrats believe that the allegations against Miller could bolster his opponent Brian Poindexter. On Tuesday, the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee announced Poindexter would be put on the committee’s “Red to Blue program.”

“Brian Poindexter is exactly the kind of leader Ohio families deserve in Congress — a union ironworker who has spent his life working alongside the people he’s running to represent,” Chairwoman Suzan DelBene said in a statement.

“Max Miller has never lived that reality. He bought his way into power, sides with corporate interests over working people, and is now facing credible allegations of domestic violence that cannot be ignored.”

The Cook Political Report rates Ohio’s 7th district as a toss-up.

Lindsay Clancy searched online about hallucinations, psychosis and the side effects of several drugs she was prescribed in the weeks before she strangled her three young children in January 2023, according to an analysis of her phone data presented at Thursday's murder trial in Massachusetts.

Clancy looked up suicide methods, bipolar disorder and insomnia at the end of December 2022 and, in January, went in search of information on postpartum depression. She also wrote a detailed note in October 2022 expressing doubts about her parenting choices, second-guessing her decision to stop breastfeeding her 8-month-old, and reconsidering plans for a fourth child.

The defense says she was in the grip of bipolar disorder and postpartum psychosis, a rare condition that can alter a woman’s sense of reality after childbirth. A forensic psychiatrist diagnosed Clancy with those conditions following the killings.

In her note, the 36-year-old former labor and delivery nurse seemed most concerned with not being able to give her youngest child the same attention as her first two, ages 3 and 5.

“I’m terrified of something happening to my kids or doing something wrong to mess up their development,” Clancy’s note read. “Our generation is inundated with information about every aspect of parenting. ... It’s insane. For the last five years, I’ve just filled my mind with all things parenting and it’s just unhealthy.”

___

EDITOR’S NOTE: This story includes discussion of suicide. If you or someone you know needs help, the national suicide and crisis lifeline in the U.S. is available by calling or texting 988.

___

Clancy has pleaded not guilty to murder charges in the deaths of Callan, Dawson and Cora Clancy. Their father found the children in the basement of the family’s home in coastal Duxbury, south of Boston. Their mother was lying in the yard after jumping out a second-story window, and remains paralyzed from the waist down.

Text messages with her then-husband, Patrick Clancy, show them juggling the routines of parenthood. Massachusetts State Police cellphone forensics expert Tim Chiappini read aloud texts between them from the day of the killings. They checked in on each other and Lindsay Clancy expressed relief that one of their children's kidneys were OK. There were also photos of the children.

“You're a good mamma,” Patrick Clancy texted, prompting Lindsay Clancy to respond with a heart and smile emoji.

Clancy's livestreamed trial has generated intense public interest, with journalists and spectators packing the courtroom as online audiences pore over the details of the tragedy.

Clancy’s attorneys do not dispute that she killed the children. But they say the jury should not hold her criminally responsible because she was mentally ill, believing she heard voices ordering her to take their lives and her own.

Prosecutors argue she was an intentional killer who contrived to get her husband out of the house by sending him to get takeout and to the pharmacy on Jan. 24, 2023, then strangled the children with exercise bands.

Prosecutor Shanan Buckingham has urged jurors not to view the trial as “a public debate about women’s mental health and how the medical system treats women.”

If convicted of murder, Clancy faces life in prison without parole. If found not guilty due to a lack of criminal responsibility, she would be committed to a state mental health facility.

Her attorneys say Clancy did everything she could to seek help: She turned to multiple outpatient providers, tried various drugs they prescribed, called a suicide hotline, went to an emergency room, and approached but wasn’t accepted into a hospital-based, full-day treatment program for women with postpregnancy mental health problems. Clancy even checked herself into a psychiatric hospital for several days.

Rather than improving, her condition worsened on the ever-remixed cocktail of psychiatric medications, some of them problematic for bipolar patients, her attorneys and family say.

Prosecutors aim to show that Clancy had access to a range of mental health services but sometimes ignored doctors' advice and stopped taking certain medications. They've brought several of her medical providers who testified she never talked about having a plan to harm herself or her children. They say she never showed signs of psychosis or mania, although she did say she was having suicidal thoughts.

The first episode of the fourth season of Ted Lasso was the most-watched premiere in the history of Apple TV.

The comedy series about an American football coach hired to work in England initially ran for three seasons on the streaming service, before being revived this month. The new season follows Lasso as he returns to coach a women’s team.

The show has divided critics, with The Independent’s Nick Hilton handing it a withering two-star review.

However, it has proved a record-breaking hit with viewers. Deadline reports that according to Nielsen data, the show’s fourth season premiere was watched for 296.6 million minutes in the United States across August 4 and 5.

That made it the most-streamed show in the country on August 5, recording more than 200 million viewing minutes.

The first episode of the fourth season of ‘Ted Lasso’ has become the most-watched premiere in the history of Apple TV ( Apple TV+ )

The new season sees Jason Sudeikis as Lasso, joined by a returning cast including Hannah Waddingham, Juno Temple, Brett Goldstein, Brendan Hunt and Jeremy Swift.

Newcomers to the cast include Tanya Reynolds, Jude Mack, Faye Marsay, Rex Hayes, Aisling Sharkey, Abbie Hern and Grant Feely.

The show originally debuted in 2020 and was nominated for 20 Emmy Awards, the most nods ever received by a first-season comedy. It won Outstanding Comedy Series, with Sudeikis taking home the Best Actor in a Comedy Series accolade, while Goldstein, who plays captain-turned-assistant-manager Roy Kent, won in the supporting actor category.

In his review of the new season for The Independent, Hilton compared the Ted Lasso revival to the Toy Story franchise.

“Toy Story 5 came out a few weeks ago and, with time to kill, I found myself going back and watching the previous four instalments in anticipation,” wrote the critic. “The first three constitute a perfect trilogy, with an ending filled with pathos and closure. And then, for some reason (answer: money) they made two more, middling additions. The same sense of gratuitous protraction is present in this reset of the Lasso universe.”

He concludes: “Americans don’t truly understand football, sure, but they do understand narrative storytelling. Ted Lasso is an all-American sporting hero in the mould of Rocky Balboa or Air Bud. The show was about bringing some of that touchy-feely shmaltz and exposing it to the rough winds of Premier League football. Can you be an eternal optimist on a cold, rainy night in Stoke? Having answered that question, the show has nowhere to go but limp on like an ageing striker whose powers are fading before their eyes.”

Women incarcerated in California were systematically failed by the prison system and were not adequately protected from sexual abuse and harassment by guards, the U.S. Department of Justice said on Thursday.

The federal investigation, which began during the Biden administration, found that California’s corrections department also failed to give victims a safe way to report sexual abuse and harassment without retaliation. Staff who were tasked with investigating the misconduct were oftentimes also accused of sexual abuse or harassment.

Two state prisons were the focus of the investigation: the Central California Women’s Facility in Chowchilla and the California Institution for Women in Chino.

Women were told to report misconduct on an online system that wasn’t confidential and that the accused officers had access to, according to Harmeet K. Dhillon, assistant attorney general for the Justice Department's Civil Rights Division.

Numerous instances were uncovered where guards regularly sexually abused incarcerated women.

The California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation did not respond to an email seeking comment.

In at least one instance, a guard was convicted of rampant abuse over roughly a decade and sentenced to 224 years in prison.

Assistant Attorney General for Civil Rights Harmeet Dhillon ( Getty )

Inmates were instructed to log complaints of mistreatment using an online portal that lacked privacy and could be viewed by accused officers, according to Harmeet K. Dhillon, assistant attorney general for the Justice Department's Civil Rights Division.

Dhillon explained that incarcerated women are "fully aware of this gap in confidentiality, and this serves as a deterrent from women reporting this misconduct." She highlighted a sergeant assigned to handle internal investigations who received a 15-year prison sentence following a guilty plea for obtaining child sexual abuse material at work.

Speaking at a Los Angeles media briefing on Thursday, Dhillon stated: "The upshot of our investigation is that California’s prison system, when it comes to women, has inadequate systems in place to deter, detect, and hold accountable rampant sexual misconduct and assault on female prisoners."

Comparable widespread offenses by federal corrections personnel against incarcerated females were previously uncovered by The Associated Press at a Dublin, California facility dubbed the "rape club." That site was ultimately shuttered after the news organization’s reporting was published.

The federal government on Thursday gave California's prison system 49 days to remediate the conditions that enabled the rampant abuse, warning that a failure to do so could result in civil litigation.

The measures include expanded camera coverage, enhanced confidential reporting channels and strengthened investigative protocol.

U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli, who was appointed by President Donald Trump as the top federal prosecutor in Los Angeles, said California has to take action.

“The State must confront the persistent failure of its own employees to prevent and address sexual abuse at these facilities,” Essayli wrote in a statement, “and the systemic breakdowns that have permitted these conditions to persist.”

Andy Burnham will consult small businesses on how the Government can best assist with their long-term planning.

It comes as his summer tour reaches Devon on Friday.

Reaffirming his unwavering support for local owners, Mr Burnham previously described independent businesses as the "beating heart of our communities".

The Prime Minister is seeking to establish a renewed working partnership between Government and small businesses following his recent announcement regarding tax cuts targeted at pubs, clubs and venues.

Offering a 20% business rates relief for hospitality sites was among Mr Burnham's initial decisions upon taking office, forming part of a broader package aimed at easing cost of living pressures.

The Prime Minister said ahead of the visit: “Local businesses are the beating heart of our communities, bringing life to the places we call home.

The Prime Minister is seeking to establish a renewed working partnership between Government and small businesses ( PA Wire )

“We are helping pubs, social clubs and live music venues by cutting their business rates, but I’ve always said there is more to do.

“I’m listening to small business owners so we can work together to deliver jobs and growth in every postcode.”

Allen Simpson, chief executive of UKHospitality, said: “Hospitality is how we will solve the youth employment crisis in every postcode and I’m pleased the Prime Minister will be seeing first hand how hotels, pubs, cafes, hotels and restaurants are the foundation of our coastal and rural communities.

“It’s encouraging that the Prime Minister is spending his first weeks in the role speaking with businesses and understanding what employers need to create jobs across the UK.

“I hope in the coming months we will see this sense of change continue.”

Mr Burnham has suggested he wants to go further with business rates relief at the Budget on October 28.

Speaking to BBC Radio 5 Live’s Wake Up To Money programme, he said: “We are going to bring forward the VAT cuts on electricity, we are bringing forward the business rate cuts for pubs, we’re going to look at business rates more broadly for high street businesses in the Budget, so there’s plenty more that we can do.”

News.title: ‘More pain’ to come after economic slowdown
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. The economy grew at a slower pace in the second quarter of the year, official figures show, under pressure from the Iran war.

The UK’s gross domestic product (GDP) expanded by 0.4pc between April and June, down from 0.6pc in the first three months of the year, according to the Office for National Statistics.

The figures underline the challenge that the conflict poses for Andy Burnham, who has pledged to deliver “growth in every postcode”.

The Prime Minister has already been warned that the economy will slow further next year if Donald Trump continues his war in the Middle East.

Treasury officials have predicted UK growth of just 0.3pc in 2027 if the Strait of Hormuz stays blocked for the rest of this year.

That is far lower than the 1.6pc predicted by the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) in March, based on assumptions made before the start of the war. Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

4) Nvidia’s AI push has echoes of Enron, says Big Short investor | Michael Burry claims chip giant is engaging in ‘circular’ financing

5) Shadow bank founder battles to stave off bankruptcy threat | Paresh Raja launches legal claim to prevent administrators from chasing him for repayment

What happened overnight
