Japan’s benchmark Nikkei 225 advanced 1.6pc to 68,601.21. In South Korea, the Kospi jumped 4pc, climbing to 6,844.65, as shares in Samsung Electronics surged 5.4pcc. Computer chipmaker SK Hynix jumped 7.1pc.

Hong Kong’s Hang Seng rose 0.3pc to 3,967.28, while the Shanghai Composite index added 0.5pc to 3,967.65.

In Australia, the S&P/ASX 200 slipped 0.4pc to 9,155.80.

Data from the US on Wednesday showed consumer prices had risen in line with analysts’ expectations in July.

Wall Street stocks were boosted on Wednesday by gains made by tech companies CoreWeave and Super Micro Computer, both of which closed up by more than 19pc.

The Nasdaq Composite ended the session up 0.5pc, with the S&P 500 up nearly 0.3pc. The Dow Jones Industrial Average finished the session marginally down.

Oil prices were little changed as investors weighed the deadlock in talks between the US and Iran over the Strait of Hormuz.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, was broadly flat at nearly $89 a barrel.

News.title: H5N1 sparks a very Australian epidemic
News.content:
H5N1 bird flu has reached Australia’s shores and is threatening to infect some of the country’s most unique wildlife.

Australasia is the last continent to be hit by the highly infectious avian influenza H5N1, a new strain of which has been circulating worldwide since 2020.

Since recording its first case in June, more than 200 wild seabirds in Australia have been infected, with fears that the highly infectious flu could quickly ‘jump’ to other species.

While H5N1 has infected animals from foxes to sea lions in other parts of the world in recent years, the epidemic now threatens some of Australia’s most iconic wildlife – many of which are found nowhere else on earth.

An Australian government assessment of more than 2,000 native species warned that nearly one in five faces a high risk from the deadly H5N1 bird flu, with hundreds of unique birds and mammals vulnerable to severe population reductions or even extinction.

Those animals include iconic species like the Tasmanian devils, quolls, and dingoes.

Other aquatic mammals, including the platypus, which is only found in Australia, are at risk of infection through contact with bird droppings in shared wetlands and coastal environments.

News.title: Selfie-seekers bring Man Utd vs Leeds match to premature end
News.content:
Aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events? Manchester United against Leeds United in Dublin always had the capacity to be lively, but try explaining the half hour that Bruno Fernandes experienced in one breath. It would be impossible.

There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.

Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.

You could say it was harmless fun but it should not have happened and the flummoxed faces that were pulled on the Manchester United bench, as an army in high-visibility jackets stood and watched it all unfold, suggested they took a dim view.

News.title: Brian Madjo, 17, electrifies Villa despite Super Cup defeat by PSG
News.content:
His team played with all the resilience and bravery that has become a trademark, epitomised by the powerful Madjo and another teenager in midfielder George Hemmings.

Emery said: “Brian has scored goals for us in pre-season and has shown his capacity to work in our idea. I am so happy because the young players were involved in our work and not playing last season.

“Of course there is still work to do but they showed they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”

This was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition. They are operating under restrictions to comply with Uefa’s financial rules and there is still the possibility of another important player leaving before the transfer deadline day.

England centre-back Ezri Konsa remains a priority target for Premier League champions Arsenal, and was absent here. Konsa, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins were all granted extended leave after their participation in the World Cup, which has done little to ease the fears of supporters over more departures. The trio will return to training this weekend.

While some outsiders are predicting a difficult season for Villa, do not bother telling Emery. He has turned putting noses out of joint into an art form since sweeping into Villa Park and with him around anything feels possible.

The Basque remains optimistic about the future and those hopes will only have been underlined by the performance of Madjo. He bullied PSG centre-back Willian Pacho for much of the evening and even managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s magician Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

News.title: Advice, cookbooks and emergency pot noodles: Your best gifts for university students
News.content:
When it comes to sending a child or grandchild off to university, it can be tempting to fill their room with every conceivable gadget.

So to help, we asked the Telegraph Recommended Community for their best gift recommendations and their suggestions ranged from desk lamps to cookery books and supermarket gift cards.

Here are the essentials worth buying.

Kitchen basics

From cupboard essentials to electrical appliances and cookbooks, most readers say they’d gift kitchen equipment.

Thinking back to his university days, reader TJ, 43, from London, says “the main essentials are around kitchen items and good long lasting food”.

“It’s nice to have some bits to cook for others as well and to make friends quickly,” he adds.

Susan, 54, from the West Midlands, agrees, recommending “basic cooking equipment” as a key staple and “distinctive cutlery, plates and cups that are easily identified”, which are particularly useful for shared accommodation.

“A box of store cupboard ingredients such as olive oil, soy, stock cubes and spices to use when cooking,” is also well-received, she says.

News.title: Everton dispatch Newcastle to give Matthias Jaissle a reality check
News.content:
Newcastle United manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the new season, as they step up their preparations against Everton at Murrayfield this evening.

Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who have lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

“It’s a challenge, a big challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle said.

“We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

“There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”

The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

He remained tight-lipped about new signings.

“Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he said.

“Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”

Jaissle said he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

“The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he said.

“The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”

Team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Ebola outbreak ‘doubling every 20 days’, warns UN chief
News.content:
Congo’s runaway Ebola outbreak is doubling in size every 20 days, according to the United Nations humanitarian chief, putting it on track to soon be the largest ever seen.

Three months after the outbreak was officially declared, the case load is expanding exponentially and many believe the true toll is far higher than recorded.

If cases continue to double at the same rate, the flare-up in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) will surpass the record West African outbreak sometime around the end of September.

Modelling by one health analytics firm already predicts there is a more than 90 per cent chance that the DRC will become the largest on record.

The two-year West African outbreak grew to more than 28,600 cases and 11,325 deaths across Sierra Leone, Liberia and Guinea from late 2013 to 2016.

This year’s outbreak centred on the DRC province of Ituri has already seen 4,449 cases and 2,061 deaths in only a few months.

News.title: Madagascar forced to divide and share mpox vaccine as epidemic takes off
News.content:
Authorities in Madagascar are being forced to split single vaccines into fifths to try to protect as many people as possible during an ongoing mpox outbreak.

The method, known as “fractional dosing”, is authorised by the World Health Organization (WHO) in emergencies when there are critical vaccine shortages, but is not routinely recommended and carries a level of risk.

Madagascar, the African island with a population of roughly 33 million people, is currently battling its largest-ever outbreak of the virus formerly known as monkeypox, with at least 4,000 cases recorded so far.

Another one million people are thought to be at risk of contracting clade 1b mpox, a fast-spreading strain of the virus that emerged from the Democratic Republic of the Congo in late 2023.

High risk groups include sex workers, young children, and people living with HIV/Aids. Medical workers are also at risk.

“Public health authorities in Madagascar have been given too few doses to protect the at-risk population; they were initially given 30,000 doses in May, and a subsequent 30,000 have just arrived at the end of July,” said Akhil Bansal, a doctor of internal medicine working on the mpox response in Madagascar and a policy fellow at the Centre for Global Development.

“However, we need to vaccinate more than one million people, so we have been “fractionally dosing”, or splitting vaccines, into fifths, to stretch the supply as far as we can.

“This is a somewhat established approach for vaccines, but even then, the number of doses we have is insufficient,” said Dr Bansal.

Sports.title: Opening day clash postponed as pitch left ‘unsuitable for playing football’ following heatwave
Sports.content:
CELTA VIGO’s opening-day LaLiga clash with Osasuna has been postponed due to FUNGUS ravaging the pitch.

The Galician side were scheduled to host the match at Balaidos Stadium this Sunday.



Celta ground staff had been working their fingers to the bone trying to rectify the outbreak that had ruined the playing surface.

And although they had made good progress, hot and dry weather conditions caused the pitch to deteriorate again.



Celta, Osasuna and the Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) all agreed to postpone the match following a LaLiga inspection.

It has now been rescheduled as a Thursday night game on August 27.

Celta said: “LaLiga agreed this morning, in coordination with the clubs and the RFEF, to postpone or find that it had to face Celta and CA Osasuna this Sunday in Abanca Balaídos due to an illness that affected the stadium’s grass, which at this time is not suitable for soccer practice.

“Last week, a technical visit was carried out by LaLiga to validate the work carried out to eradicate the disease that affected the grass and certify that the field met the quality and safety parameters set for sports practice.

“The climatic conditions of the last two days produced an adverse effect on the evolution that was close to the game and led to the decision to suspend or terminate.

“The tickets issued for this match against Osasuna remain fully valid for the new schedule, so it will not be necessary to carry out any additional processing.

“Celta regrets the inconvenience and inconvenience that this decision may cause to all the fans who have organized their day to accompany the team at the start of the competition, and appreciates your understanding in this exceptional circumstance.”

Celta will now get their league season underway with a trip to Valencia on August 22.

The Spanish side’s squad features ex-Liverpool flop Iago Aspas, former Chelsea defender Marcos Alonso, and out-of-favour Manchester United goalkeeper Altay Bayindir, who joined on loan last week.

Celta finished fifth in LaLiga last season and will play in the Europa League this term.

Sports.title: England legend Steven Gerrard, 46, handed biggest TV role yet ahead of new Premier League season

Sports.title: West Ham bans much mocked half-and-half scarves from stadium for new season as fans are warned they will be confiscated
Sports.content:
WEST Ham bosses have banned much mocked half-and-half scarves for good.

The divisive neckwear — bearing the names of both home and away teams — are sold outside grounds across the country and are popular with tourists.

But die-hard fans despise them, and they are sometimes outlawed for one-off games against rivals as displaying away colours at the home end poses safety risks.



The Hammers, newly relegated to the Championship, have posted warning signs at their City of ­London Stadium.



They state: “West Ham United would like to remind supporters that half-and-half scarves and any items displaying the colours or crests of both clubs are permanently banned inside London Stadium.

“This policy applies at all fixtures.

“Supporters arriving with half-and-half scarves purchased from unofficial sellers will be required to hand them over to security staff at the security checkpoints and these scarves will not be returned.



“Fans wishing to purchase a scarf for the game are encouraged to visit the official West Ham United Stadium Store where a full range of official merchandise is available ahead of kick-off.”

The rule was brought in for the Hammers’ 3-1 League Cup win over Portsmouth last weekend.

The move divided fans. West Ham nut John Hayes told The Sun: “The scarves are for the tourists who take away from the match atmosphere created by die-hard fans, who are often priced out of attending by the rubberneckers.

“Having a rival club’s crest on view in the home end sparks all sorts of problems.



“These scarves deserve going into the bin — with hydration breaks.”

But Arsenal fan Frank DuPont hit back: “Football is meant to be for everyone.

Tourists spend the most in the club shops, and picking up a half-and-half scarf from a street vendor is not going to damage the match experience for fussy season ticket holders.”

Previous West Ham games where the scarves have been banned include last season’s home match against Tottenham Hotspur.

Sports.title: Arsenal and Galatasaray hold stunning transfer talks as ‘Victor Osimhen’s name comes up’ with two Gunners stars
Sports.content:
ARSENAL face a fight to sign Victor Osimhen – if they decide to press ahead with a move for the Galatasaray striker.

The Gunners are currently in talks with the Turkish club as they look to offload Ethan Nwaneri and Gabriel Martinelli.



And Osimhen’s name is said to have come up in those discussions between the two clubs.

But it is understood that Galatasaray are determined to keep hold of their star striker and do not want to sell him.



The Turkish giants have already rejected an offer of £111million this summer from an unnamed club, believed to be Saudi Arabian side Al-Hilal.

Arsenal would find it hard to soften that stance, although they can take heart from Newcastle initially being adamant Bruno Guimaraes would not be sold.

Osimhen is a player that the Gunners have looked at in the past, including when Edu was their sporting director.

The 27-year-old scored 22 goals in all competitions last season and helped Galatasaray win the Turkish top flight.

The Gunners are in the market for a marquee attacker this summer, but failed in their attempts to sign Morgan Rogers and Vinicius Junior.

The club are also looking to offload players, with Martinelli and Nwaneri offered to Galatasaray.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The Turkish side have indicated they would pay around £38m for Martinelli, yet it is unclear if the Brazilian would be happy to move there.

Nwaneri, 19, is thought to prefer a move to Germany – if he leaves Arsenal – and is of interest to both Borussia Dortmund and RB Leipzig.

Dortmund have long admired the midfielder and were keen on him last summer, before he signed a five-year contract at the Emirates.

Arsenal hope to offload striker Gabriel Jesus and Napoli are currently the favorites to land the Brazilian.



Fabio Vieira hopes to return to Hamburg after spending last season on loan there, but a fee is proving hard to agree.

Reiss Nelson is a target for West Ham and the Hammers are hopeful of striking a deal, despite being in the Championship.

Sports.title: Arsenal files: Pre-season clash cancelled due to TYPHOON as famous referee retires on Emirates pitch
Sports.content:
ARSENAL fans will dominate the stands in this Sunday’s Community Shield against Manchester City.

The Gunners have been handed over 7,000 extra tickets to the curtain-raiser after Man City failed to sell out their full allocation at the Principality Stadium.



Arsenal were originally handed 25,218 tickets for the fixture, but are now expected to have close to 35,000 fans in Cardiff for the game.

A sea of red is expected in the stands, with Arsenal’s allocation stretching around almost 75 per cent of the seats available to supporters.



The game is being played in Wales due to a concert at Wembley Stadium this weekend, yet Arsenal’s players may feel like they are playing at the Emirates thanks to the enormous travelling support.

Fabregas’ sly return

Cesc Fabregas couldn’t wait to return to the Emirates Stadium on Wednesday night for Arsenal vs Como.

So much so that the former Gunners midfielder was in the stands for Arsenal’s pre-season defeat to Borussia Dortmund three days prior.

Fabregas’ Como side spent the week training in the UK and Fabregas made a point of coming to the Emirates to watch the Dortmund game before returning again on Wednesday.

It wasn’t the only time he has watched a game from the stands in recent years.

Fabregas was also present for Arsenal’s famous victory over Real Madrid in the Champions League two seasons ago.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The retired midfielder has an unusual relationship with Arsenal supporters given his move to Chelsea late in his career.

But the Emirates faithful ensured he was given a warm welcome during Wednesday night’s 1-1 draw with Como.

New backroom staff member

Arsenal have made further changes to their medical department by hiring Yeray Abreu Martinez.



The Spaniard is a strength and conditioning coach, who specialises in the rehab of players.

Most recently, he had been working with Saudi Arabian club Al Ittihad but he has now joined the Gunners.

In a statement on social media, Martinez said: “Proud and grateful to be part of the Arsenal family.

“A new chapter that I embrace with great commitment and ambition, looking forward to what’s ahead in this great project.”

Arsenal made sweeping changes to their medical team this summer and Martinez is one of several new faces.



Consultant Joaquin Acedo – who has known Arteta for decades – has played a key role in the revamp.

Teens’ typhoon trouble

Arsenal’s youngsters saw part of their pre-season preparations CANCELLED due to a typhoon.

The Gunners’ Under-17 side had been taking part in the Shanghai Future Stars Cup in China and made it to the final after a penalty shootout win over Shanghai U17s.

Arsenal were due to face China’s U17s in the final, but the match was scrapped due to dangerous weather conditions.



The Young Guns were named joint-winners of the tournament after the game was scuppered by the typhoon.

Highly-rated teenager Jaden Maghoma won the golden boot after netting four times during the tournament.

Arsenal’s travelling squad also included rising star Luis Munoz, Ethan Nwaneri’s brother Emerson Nwaneri, and Mikel Arteta’s son Gabriel Arteta.

Tzol the rage

Christos Tzolis made his debut in the Premier League five years ago against…Arsenal.



Tzolis and his Norwich team suffered a 1-0 loss at the Emirates on September 11, 2021.

Had the Canaries won, manager Mikel Arteta would have been under massive pressure as it would have been a fourth successive top-flight loss for the Spaniard.

Arsenal scored with a scrappy 66th-minute winner from Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang, with the visitors believing that VAR missed a handball and Tzolis, a £9million arrival from PAOK, was replaced a couple of minutes later by Daniel Farke.

Norwich’s former sporting director Stuart Webber recalled: “Christos scored twice against Bournemouth in the League Cup so he started at Arsenal.

“We’d lost the first three games of the season. We’d lost against Liverpool at home, Manchester City away, Leicester at home.



“But they’d also lost the first three games of the season.

“Arteta, in that game, was under huge pressure. You’d have to ask them, but I’m pretty sure if we’d rocked up and beat them, it would’ve been a problem.

“I remember Nicolas Pepe was playing for them. Brandon Williams had him in his pocket. It was the scrappiest 1-0 game. Let’s say their goal ricocheted off a handball.

“A fair result would’ve been his draw, but yes, Christos made his debut in the Premier League that day.”



Five years later, Tzolis will be looking to make his Premier League debut for Arsenal against Coventry next Friday.

Webber added: “I’m delighted he’s gone and done what he’s done. He’s just a really good guy who cares a lot. I think it hurt him that it didn’t quite work out with us.”

Ref’s farewell

Assistant referee Sian Massey-Ellis ended her officiating career at the Emirates Stadium on Sunday.

The lineswoman announced last week that she would be hanging up her flag and had a final send-off in North London for Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup.

Her final match was celebrated behind the scenes at the stadium before she had one last outing ahead of a move to an FA position.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Massey-Ellis has officiated in over 150 Premier League matches since making her debut in 2010.

She is set to become The FA‘s Senior Manager for Women Referees from September, where she will support and develop female officials across the country.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo shows off dramatic new look days after marrying Georgina Rodriguez

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola copycats have been ruining the EFL slams veteran boss Tony Mowbray
Sports.content:
PEP GUARDIOLA copycats have been ruining EFL football.

That is the damning verdict from veteran boss Tony Mowbray as Blackburn travel to Wolves tonight for the Championship curtain-raiser.



And Mowbray, 62, insists a generation of bosses have been brainwashed into over-complicating the game with total-football tactics their players cannot pull off.

The Rovers boss told SunSport: “Pep Guardiola changed the landscape of football.



“People say it almost spoilt the game because everybody wants to play like Pep — but we can’t all play like him.

“In 2012, he had a formidable team at Barcelona with Xavi and Iniesta, a generation full of talent playing a false nine.

“A generation of coaches have come through inspired by him, inverting full-backs and playing overloads in different areas.

“And yet every week in lower leagues we see teams giving pathetic goals away by the goalie trying to play a little triangle in his box.

“At teams lower down, it’s much more difficult. It’s easier to press than to be the team with the ball.

“We can’t all play like Pep — you need a fusion of football and pragmatism.”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Mowbray believes the era of blind possession copycats is finally shifting into a far more practical, diverse age of football.

Mowbray said: “I think it’s riveting. Guardiola’s left now, and I think the game will resort back — not back to the 80s where everybody just has a striker and a little guy fast over the top.

“But I think it will become more diverse. More teams will be playing off the front and beating the press.

“It will become more pragmatic as well. I think there’s going to be a really special, good era of football.

“I love the game, all aspects of it. I can see the benefits of having a big centre-forward who can bring it in or flick it on, playing over the top of all these pressing teams who understand where the pressing lines are.



“When teams commit so many men to a press to win the ball high up, if you play over it, you’re two passes away and you can score. I think that’s really thought-provoking.

“That’s why I love the job of being a coach — analysing the teams we’re going to play and seeing whether we are going to kick every goal kick long today, or build from the back with four or five men and play through their lines. I like the idea of a team who can do both. A fusion of football.”

That obsession with trendy coaching metrics and extra tactical staff almost made Mowbray fall out of love with the game.

In early 2024, his world was turned upside down when forced to step down from Birmingham following a bowel cancer diagnosis.

And after undergoing surgery and treatment, Mowbray admits modern football’s push toward technical directors interfering with squad selection made him question returning.



He said: “I started thinking I wasn’t enjoying where football was going.

“I remember once trying to sign a very young Gerard Pique for Hibs on loan from Manchester United.

“I was at a petrol station, looked at my phone that was ringing and it said Alex Ferguson. I didn’t know whether to keep filling my car or take the call.

“I stopped and answered. He couldn’t let me have Pique but told me, ‘I’d advise you to have total control. The only way to succeed is to have control so players know who the boss is.’



“When I was at West Brom against Sir Alex, he’d come in for a drink and talk about control. That’s gone now.

“There are too many layers. Do I want to get told by a technical director who to pick or why players ran too hard? It’s about trust.”

That search for respect drew Mowbray back to Ewood Park following his recovery.

Following a short interim spell at West Brom last season, a homecoming at Blackburn gave him what Sir Alex insisted on… freedom to manage.

Mowbray said: “The job has become harder for coaches. I’ve always felt the manager needs to manage and pick the team.



“I found integrity and honesty in this ownership model. They look me in the eye and let me get on with it. The respect is there.

“There are different layers from when I was here before, but I don’t want total control. I want to do it together.”

Mowbray points to Blackburn’s academy products as proof that passing quality and direct power must coexist.



Crystal Palace and England midfielder Adam Wharton came through the ranks during Mowbray’s last spell between 2017 and 2022.

He said: “Adam was only 14 or 15 — but he’d train with the first team because he was so special with the ball.

“Jon Dahl Tomasson, who followed me, gave him his debut and Adam allowed the team to play an amazing passing game.

“I love seeing that, but I see the benefits of a big centre-forward who can bring it in or flick it on, playing over pressing teams.

“It’s a fusion of football. You have to figure it out.”



Despite his wariness of all the layers of analysts and technical staff in football, do not brand Mowbray a dinosaur.

He said: “I like data pointing us to the right players.

“There might be a winger in Belgium’s second division putting in the most crosses and I’d never know until data points at him.

“Then your wisdom correlates whether he can step up to Championship level and if he has the right personality to fit your group. Ultimately, data cannot tell you that.”

Mowbray admits his time off while fighting illness left him climbing the walls at home.



And with his children flying the nest for university, the family hit a major turning point.

Mowbray revealed: “I was driving everyone mad at home! Walking the dog was the highlight of my day.

“My kids are older now. One is 19 and flying off to college in America. We’re at a crossroads as a family because everyone’s flying the nest.



“How relieved is my wife Amber that I got back to work? She’s happy. She knows football is my driving force.

“She’s made so many sacrifices and deserves a medal.”

Back at Ewood Park, the thrill of managing still burns.

Mowbray said: “Seven months at home with the health pressure, I had dark moods.

“People asked if I looked at retirement — but my fire still burns. Why do I love it? Because you’re dealing with 30 individuals every day.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Some feel they’re the best player in town, asking, ‘Why am I not playing?’ Others are quiet and shy, yet they’re the best technicians, and you try to bring personality out of them.

“It’s an amazing job. You need trust and empathy. Computers are great, but you need a human touch.”

Sports.title: Wilfried Zaha training at Premier League club six weeks after becoming unemployed
Sports.content:
WILFRIED ZAHA has been using Crystal Palace’s training ground to stay sharp this summer.

The winger, 33, scored 90 goals in 458 appearances across two spells with the Eagles – the second of which ended in 2023.



And excitement has been growing among Palace fans around Zaha potentially returning for a third stint.

But SunSport understands that Zaha’s sessions at Copers Cope Road are only part of an informal arrangement.



Palace agreed to grant Zaha personal use of the facilities until he finds a new club.

And a longer-term deal that could see the former Manchester United star lace up for Palace again is not under consideration.

Zaha posted a video montage showing him dribbling past training dummies and firing into netted goals on Thursday.

The comments section was chock-full of Palace fans trying to persuade him to come back.

But the decision rests with the club, who have already signed winger Dwight McNeil this summer and are weighing up a swoop for Solly March.

Zaha has been a free agent since his Galatasaray contract expired at the end of June.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The Ivory Coast international scored 10 goals in 43 games for the Turkish side but was shipped out on loan twice during his time there.

His loan at Lyon was cut short halfway through the season after six goalless appearances.

And the French club’s manager at the time, Pierre Sage, is now in charge of Palace.

Zaha then spent a year and a half on loan at Charlotte, scoring 13 goals in 48 games.

Sports.title: Arsenal handed chance of stunning Victor Osimhen swap transfer with talks opened
Sports.content:
Arsenal handed chance of stunning Victor Osimhen swap transfer with talks opened

Arsenal are scouring the market for a world-class forward after missing out on Vinicius Junior and with Julian Alvarez too expensive - and Victor Osimhen has emerged as an option

View 2 Images Victor Osimhen could leave Galatasaray this summer (Image: Arife Karakum/Getty Images)

Arsenal have reportedly held talks with Galatasaray over the possibility of signing striker Victor Osimhen. The Turkish club initiated discussions over Arsenal duo Gabriel Martinelli and Ethan Nwaneri, but Osimhen has also been raised, with a stunning swap deal now a consideration.

‌



The Gunners have been on the lookout for a world-class forward in the summer transfer window and previously enquired about Real Madrid star Vinicius Junior. The Brazilian ended up signing a new contract with Real, while fellow target Julian Alvarez is proving difficult to land.

‌



Alvarez is valued at over £100million by Atletico Madrid and is also of interest to Barcelona, forcing Arsenal to look elsewhere. Now an intriguing option has emerged during sporting director Andrea Berta's discussions with Galatasaray over two possible sales.

‌



Martinelli and Nwaneri are among the players Mikel Arteta is willing to offload this summer and Galatasaray are interested in both. According to The Telegraph, the Turkish giants have offered £38.4m for Martinelli and are also exploring a move for Nwaneri, who spent last season on loan with Marseille.

‌



During these talks, it is reported that a move for Osimhen to Arsenal was proposed. The 27-year-old Nigeria international has been one of Europe's most prolific goalscorers in recent years and has consistently been linked with a move to the Premier League, including to Tottenham this summer.

He only joined Galatasaray permanently from Napoli last summer for €75m (£64m) following a successful loan spell. Osimhen has 59 goals and 16 assists in 74 appearances for the club and is under contract until June 2029.

Martinelli appears poised to leave Arsenal after seven years, 62 goals and 278 appearances at the club. He has entered the final year of his contract and has been made available for a transfer alongside Gabriel Jesus, who is of interest to Napoli.

‌



View 2 Images Arsenal are ready to sell Gabriel Martinelli (Image: PA Wire)

Leandro Trossard (Besiktas), Jakub Kiwior (Porto), Karl Hein (Werder Bremen) and Christian Norgaard (Everton) are the only players have left the defending Premier League champions for transfer fees this summer. And Arteta knows the importance of sales to help free up funds and space in the squad for new additions.

“There is more that we want to do, because every time we have an opportunity to improve the squad and bring more quality and depth, we need to do that,” Arteta said after the 1-1 draw with Como on Wednesday. “We’re actively trying to do so – the thing is, in the market, it doesn’t just depend on you, and we’re very clear on that.

‌



“The will and the desire of the club is unquestionable, but we cannot promise that we’re going to do it because it doesn’t only depend on us.”

He added: “For the margins to improve, there are very few players in the market that are available to do that and bring more quality to the club,. But again, we’re actively looking to improve that and we’re going to try.”

Marcus Rashford has returned to Manchester United for pre-season training this week after his loan spell with Barcelona came to an end

Manchester United legend John O'Shea says it'll be a straightforward conversation between Michael Carrick and Marcus Rashford ahead of his return to the first-team setup. The England forward is set to return to the fold for Carrick, despite spending the last 18 months plying his trade elsewhere.

‌



Barcelona turned down the chance to Rashford permanently after his loan stint at the Nou Camp, and he reported back for pre-season training with the Reds earlier this week. There was still uncertainty about his future at Old Trafford leading up to the pre-season clash with Leeds United, but O'Shea is convinced his former colleague is man to get the best out of the England international.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick confirms Man Utd's Marcus Rashford plan as transfer reality becomes clear
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick confirms Man Utd's Marcus Rashford plan as transfer reality becomes clear

Marcus Rashford has returned to Manchester United following loan spells with Aston Villa and Barcelona as Michael Carrick prepares to reintegrate him into the squad

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford is back in the Manchester United picture

Michael Carrick insists Marcus Rashford still has plenty to offer Manchester United this season with it now looking increasingly likely he will stay at Old Trafford.

‌



The England international hasn't played for his boyhood club since December 2024, when he was frozen out by former manager Ruben Amorim. Since then, he has had loan spells with Aston Villa and then spent last season with Barcelona.

‌



It was expected that he would secure a permanent move to the Camp Nou, but their decision to sign Anthony Gordon meant they opted against triggering his £26million clause.

‌



He now returns to United, where he could make his return, ironically, against Amorim's AC Milan this weekend. The Manchester Evening News report both sides believe it is most likely he will remain at his parent club and Carrick is confident he will be a positive presence in his squad.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"He's a very good player, and I think if you're going to have a career over 10 or 15 years, there's going to be times when things go in a direction and maybe a different direction," he said.

‌



"I think there are ups and downs, and that doesn't judge you as a one-off kind of judgment. It's what happens over time, and now we're in a positive place as a group, and Marcus can offer us so much. He has done, and he can do again, so in that respect, it's quite exciting."

Had Amorim stayed in charge, it is inconceivable that the burnt bridges would have been able to be mended, but Carrick has a history with Rashford and has helped to smooth the process.

And while Carrick stopped short of definitively confirming he will stay at United, he described him as 'our player' and said he is being treated the same as anyone else within his squad.

‌



View 2 Images Rashford has not played for Manchester United since December 2024 (Image: Getty Images)

"He's our player, he came back Sunday night, he arrived with Kobbie [Mainoo], and Lisandro [Martinez] came the day after, and he's part of the group like anybody else. He came in, he's trained really well.

"I've known him a long time, like I've known some of the others a long time, so I don't treat him any different to anybody else, but it's been good to have him around the group again this week. So I'm really positive with that."

‌



Carrick added that he was confident the returning Rashford would bring something new to his options and help balance the squad for the upcoming Premier League campaign.

He added: "We're really calm, we just treat it like anybody else coming into the group and there's obviously this slight twist that he knows the club as well as anybody and that's a real positive.

‌



"He's been here all his career, all his life before the last 18 months or so, to understand what it means. That side of things is natural, that's a given. I know he's got history, but I've got history with a number of the players as well, so that doesn't make that a unique situation at all and treat him as exactly like any other player.

"Bringing him into the group and carrying on as normal brings the good things that we haven't got, and we want to get that balance with every individual player, and Marcus has come back and he's in good form, and it's been good to have him around this week."

Sports.title: Michael Carrick tells Man Utd owners exactly what he needs in rest of transfer window
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick tells Man Utd owners exactly what he needs in rest of transfer window

Manchester United have gone a month without announcing a transfer in the summer window and manager Michael Carrick has urged the hierarchy to get deals over the line

View 2 Images Michael Carrick is keen for new players at Manchester United (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Michael Carrick has sent a clear message to the Manchester United hierarchy by telling them to "keep pushing" for more transfers this summer.

‌



United have signed Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, from Aston Villa and Chelsea respectively, to strengthen their midfield, while Karl Darlow arrived from Leeds on a free transfer to become the back-up goalkeeper. But their total expenditure of £85million lags way behind their Premier League rivals.

‌



It has now been a month since United announced a new signing and, with just 19 days left until the transfer deadline on September 1 and nine until United's first game of the 2026/27 season, Carrick has made his feelings clear.

‌



"I think we've got a pretty good balance in all when you lay the squad out, but we would like more, we need to keep pushing for more," he told the Manchester Evening News.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



"There's one or two areas where we'd like to improve and we feel that there's the possibility to improve, but again, that needs to be something that we can do that makes us better and improves the group, whether that's quality or whether that's a little bit of depth. That's something we've got to manage. That's pretty obvious."

Carrick wants to sign a left-back to compete with Luke Shaw, with Newcastle's Lewis Hall the top target, as well as another central midfielder. His squad only had to compete in the Premier League following his arrival as interim boss in January to replace Ruben Amorim and Carrick knows the upcoming campaign will be more demanding, with United back in the Champions League and cup competitions.

This summer has seen huge transfer fees become even more normalised, with Morgan Rogers, Elliot Anderson and Sandro Tonali all moving for £100m or more. Remarkably, United's record transfer remains the £89m they paid Juventus for Paul Pogba in 2016.

‌



View 2 Images Andrey Santos has impressed Michael Carrick since his £50m transfer (Image: Michael Campanella/Getty Images)

Asked if United may need to break that record this summer, Carrick said: "A little bit depends on what position that is and what you've got and what dynamics you need at certain points. Sometimes you do need that if it's the right player.

"Again, it's not purely on money, the money doesn't guarantee you, it needs to be the right player and a better player for what we've got. It's something [that] over time we need to be pushing to look to enhance the squad all the time in different ways."

‌



Carrick has been delighted by the impact that Santos, in particular, has made since joining for £50m from Chelsea. And he stressed that communication with director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada remains good.

"It's constant communication of where, what work we need to do, where we want to improve," he said. "We're pretty clear in the messages that we need to keep pushing and there's certain things that we want to try and do, but it needs to be right as well."

Sports.title: Man Utd handed Lewis Hall transfer update as Newcastle close in on full-back agreement
Sports.content:
Man Utd handed Lewis Hall transfer update as Newcastle close in on full-back agreement

Manchester United manager Michael Carrick wants the club to sign a new left-back before the summer transfer window closes and Newcastle's Lewis Hall is top of their wish list

View 2 Images Lewis Hall remains a Newcastle player for now (Image: Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images)

Manchester United's pursuit of Lewis Hall could be given renewed hope after Newcastle made a breakthrough in the transfer market. Hall is United's No.1 target as they chase a left-back this summer and a development on Tyneside may have caught their eye.

‌



United manager Michael Carrick is keen to add some competition for Luke Shaw ahead of the start of the 2026/27 season. Academy graduate Harry Amass has been told he is free to leave, Diego Leon hasn't kicked on as hoped, Diego Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui are more comfortable at right-back and Patrick Dorgu is better further forward on the left.

‌



United have been monitoring Hall for some time and believe he is the perfect long-term successor to Shaw, who is entering his 13th season at the club. A previous approach was firmly rejected by Newcastle, who are determined not to sell Hall after waving goodbye to Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes.

‌



The 21-year-old still has three years left on his contract following a £28million move from Chelsea two years ago, putting the Magpies in a strong negotiating position. It is believed they value the defender at £60m.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Despite Newcastle's reluctance to do business, United may be encouraged by a report from The Athletic, which says they have made significant progress in talks with Benfica for full-back Amar Dedic.

Bosnia and Herzegovina international Dedic is expected to cost Newcastle around €35m (£30m) and will become the first signing of the Matthias Jaissle era. The 23-year-old is primarily a right-back, but is also capable of playing at left-back with Tino Livramento closing in on a return to full fitness.

Newcastle have been desperate for defensive reinforcements and to bolster a squad depleted by the departures of Kieran Trippier, Emil Krafth and Matt Targett this summer.

‌



Newcastle have banked over £250m from the sales of Gordon, Tonali and Guimaraes and their hierarchy are under pressure to ensure Eddie Howe's successor has a competitive squad come the start of the campaign. As such, they have so far been unwilling to discuss an exit for Hall.

View 2 Images Amar Dedic is expected to leave Benfica for Newcastle (Image: Carlos Rodrigues/Getty Images)

What could change that stance is Hall himself. The Sun reported this week that Hall is keen to leave for the Red Devils. If he were to agitate for a move, like Alexander Isak famously did last summer to leave for Liverpool, it could leave Newcastle with little choice.

‌



United have signed Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa and Andrey Santos from Chelsea to strengthen their midfield, while Karl Darlow has arrived on a free transfer to become the back-up goalkeeper. But a left-back and another central midfielder are considered must haves by Carrick.

If Hall proves unattainable then United will pursue other targets. Club Brugge's £30m-rated Joaquin Seys another option, along with Jorge Salinas of Racing Santander, who would cost around £14m.

Sports.content:
Man Utd star Youri Tielemans issues grovelling apology over comments in interview

Manchester United summer arrival Youri Tielemans has been forced to apologise after his comments following the cross Premier League move

View 2 Images Youri Tielemans joined Man United in the summer. (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United midfielder Youri Tielemans has been forced to apologise following his comments after leaving Aston Villa. The summer arrival claimed that the Red Devils were above his former employers, whom he helped back to European silverware with their Europa League triumph.

‌



The Red Devils made the move for the 29-year-old during the summer as they triggered the £35million release clause within his contract. Tielemans ended his three year spell in the West Midlands and arrived as part of the reinforcements in Michael Carrick's midfield, a problem position at Old Trafford in recent years.

‌



However, Tielemans sparked anger with his comments in his first extended sit-down with journalists as the conclusion to United's pre-season preparations looms closer.

Sports.title: Who is Brian Madjo? The Aston Villa wonderkid tipped to be England's Harry Kane successor
Sports.content:
One game, one goal. That's all it takes for a young striker to put themselves on the list of potential Harry Kane successors, such is the concern among England fans over who'll lead the line once their captain's powers wane.

A despondent Kane admitted in the aftermath of England's heartbreaking defeat to Argentina last month that he doesn't know if he'll play at the next World Cup in 2030. By then, he'll be 36 and likely not the force he was in North America.

That's why England need to start the search for his successor. Step forward: Brian Madjo.

At 17 years and six months old, starting a match of UEFA Super Cup's magnitude is enough to get people talking. But his emphatic first-time finish against European champions Paris Saint-Germain has sparked feverish excitement at Villa Park.

‌



The Aston Villa wonderkid - we can safely label him that now - held off Willian Pacho with relative ease at the back post before firing past Matvey Safonov with his weaker left foot. Although it wouldn't send Villa on their way to victory, it was a goal that announced himself on the European stage.

EFL 2026-27 predictions with Championship winners decided as West Ham and Wolves discover fate READ MORE :

But talent spotters have known about him for years. Born in Enfield, north London, Madjo moved to Luxembourg with his Cameroonian parents at a young age. His dad, Guy, was a striker himself and played for several EFL clubs.

After playing in the academies of Luxembourgish sides Marisca Mersch and Racing Union, French club Metz - then in the top flight - came calling in 2023. He made his debut last season aged 16 and played a further four games for their first team in the first half of the 2025-26 campaign.

‌



Meanwhile, Madjo won three caps for Luxembourg at senior level. But thanks to FIFA's rules on player allegiance, he was able to switch to England, as those caps had come in friendlies.

Madjo has since played nine times for England's under-17s, scoring four goals and providing one assist. At club level, however, his move to Aston Villa wasn't as simple.

Is Brain Madjo the next big thing? Have your say in the comments section.

5 View 5 Images Brian Madjo scored on his Aston Villa debut in the UEFA Super Cup (Image: Aston Villa/Aston Villa FC via Getty Images) 5 View 5 Images He's already being tipped as a long-term replacement for Harry Kane (Image: Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images)

‌



Signed for £10million in January, Madjo initially couldn't play in competitive fixtures due to FIFA's rules on the international transfers of minors. The 17-year-old's transfer was considered an international one due to his appearances for Luxembourg, whereas Villa argued that he was English - given that he was born there and is a UK citizen.

The Premier League club took the dispute to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) and won their legal battle earlier this month. That allowed Madjo to be involved in Wednesday's Super Cup in Salzburg and Unai Emery gave him the nod in the absence of Ollie Watkins.

Afforded extra time off after being part of England's squad at the World Cup, Watkins suddenly faces a fight to be in Emery's first-choice starting line-up. At 30, though, Watkins will still fancy his chances of being Kane's successor himself.

View 5 Images Brian Madjo has enjoyed an impressive pre-season with Aston Villa (Image: Dan Istitene/Getty Images)

‌



Yet his situation at Villa Park could soon be replicated with England. Former Villa striker Stan Collymore reckons that a senior call-up isn't far away. "I guarantee he'll be fast tracked into U21s then seniors by the end of the season," Collymore posted on X during Wednesday's clash.

"England are struggling for strikers, out and out No.9s. We aren't producing them at any senior or youth level. So Madjo (he's raw but his physical dominance of two world class central defenders WILL warrant a look by England scouting analysis) potentially being fast tracked simply addresses a problem.

"Is he good enough? God knows. Is one friendly judgement overkill (he's been very good in pre season and one of Europe's best managers deemed him ready enough to play against the European Champions), no I don't think so. There's a gap in England and looking at him is just common sense."

View 5 Images Brian Madjo has switched his allegiance to England from Luxembourg (Image: Frederic Scheidemann - The FA/The FA via Getty Images)

‌



After full-time, Villa right-back Matty Cash was asked about Madjo and described his team-mate as a 'beast'. "All pre-season he's put his body around, scored goals," Cash explained.

"And then tonight he had a few chances as well. He had the header where he probably could've scored and then a good finish. Really happy for him and 17 is still so young. He'll be delighted."

Last year, Luxembourg's technical director, Manuel Cardoni, likened him to Romelu Lukaku - but insists that Madjo can be better. "His profile is similar but, even if we are keeping our feet on the ground, Brian has a more complete profile," Cardoni claimed.

"He is good in tight spaces, really good in terms of positional play. He is also good in terms of going in behind, and he can also feed the ball with both feet. He has huge room for growth."

‌



Plenty of excitement, then. But to offer context for how early we are into Madjo's career, you can't even buy him on Fantasy Premier League yet.

Nevertheless, there'll already be expectation on his shoulders when Villa kick-off their Premier League campaign away to Brighton next Sunday. And with the September-October international break not far away, who knows what Thomas Tuchel is thinking?

Madjo could be rubbing shoulders with Kane sooner than we think - or even breathing down his neck.

Sports.title: Gay out for duck as Pakistan impress against County Select XI
Sports.content:
England opening batter Emilio Gay was out for a duck as Pakistan made a strong start to their tour against a Professional County Club Select XI.

Concerns over Gay's fitness for England's first Test against Pakistan, which starts on August 19, were allayed by the left-hander's inclusion for the game at Beckenham, but he made the worst possible start.

The 27-year-old, who had suffered a shoulder issue playing for Durham last week, was caught off the bowling of Mohammad Abbas by Salan Agha at second slip, having failed to score from his 12 balls faced.

PCCSXI would go on to be bowled out for 305, with captain Tom Haines, Caleb Falconer and Saif Zaib contributing half-centuries before Matthew Fisher, who is in England's 16-player squad for the first two Tests against Pakistan, made a crucial unbeaten 62 batting at 10.

James Rew, who made his England Test debut against New Zealand in June, was also dismissed cheaply as he fell for just four to Abbas.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England Test captain Joe Root explains why he has removed the curfew that was previously imposed on his team.

Abbas (3-37) and Mohammad Ali (3-23) were the pick of the Pakistan bowlers, while Khurram Shahzad (2-55) also chipped with a couple of wickets despite being more expensive.

There was also a wicket apiece for Aamer Jamal (1-32) and Ali Usman (1-38).

Pakistan then put themselves in a strong position in the three-day contest by reaching 44-0 at the close, with Azan Awais (15*) and Imam-ul-Haq (26*) seeing out the final 13 overs of the day.

Fisher was economical as he went for just seven runs from his four overs, while the other PCCSXI player who is in England's Test squad, spinner Shoaib Bashir, bowled two overs at the end of the day.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England selector Marcus North reflects on the latest decisions around the Test side and explains the involvement of Stephen Fleming.

Both sides are fielding more than XI players in the match, with Pakistan attempting to give as many of their touring squad as possible match practice ahead of Tests at Headingley, Lord's and Edgbaston.

England will be led captained by Joe Root following his reappointment as captain after Ben Stokes retired from international cricket during the final Test of the 2-1 series defeat to New Zealand in June.

England also have a new head coach in Stephen Fleming, who has replaced Brendon McCullum but is not taking charge of the side during the Pakistan series, for which Marcus Trescothick will be in interim charge.

Sports.title: McIlroy makes woeful start to FedExCup Playoffs as Spieth shares early lead
Sports.content:
Rory McIlroy made a woeful start to the FedExCup Playoffs as he shot four-over par opening round at the FedEx St. Jude Championship in Memphis.

Playing for the first time since finishing tied for 40th at The Open at Royal Birkdale almost a full month ago, McIlroy was level par going into the final three holes before a disastrous streak left him towards the rear of the field.

Dropped shots at 16 and 17 were followed by a double bogey at TPC Southwind's final hole, which came after McIlroy found the water with his tee shot to the closing par four.

The 74 left McIlroy nine shots adrift of the early leaders, with American duo Jordan Spieth and Michael Thorbjornsen setting the early pace with 65s.

England's Tommy Fleetwood, who was paired with Spieth, was a shot off that mark after opening up with a 66 that included a delightful chip in for eagle at the par-five third hole.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tommy Fleetwood produced this eagle on third hole at the FedEx St. Jude Championship.

Fleetwood said: "I feel good. I didn't really play very good in the practice days. Game's not really been that great. I've been showing a lot, like some good and some really not so good.

"Hit it great off the tee today. Still my iron play was iffy, but I did a good job of managing it for the most part. Still hit some really good shots, and you can never underestimate how good - I think shooting under par on this golf course is very good."

World No 1 Scottie Scheffler, who played alongside McIlroy in the marquee group for the opening two rounds, put himself in a solid position by delivering a 68.

Scheffler said: "I felt like I hit a lot of quality shots with my irons.I did a good job of being patient and not trying to force it too much.

"I feel like I was right on the edge of having a good day, kind of all day is how I would describe it. So, I felt like patience-wise, I did a pretty good job."

Fleetwood had European company towards the top of the leaderboard, with Ludvig Aberg and Sepp Straka both joining Scheffler on two-under.

McIlroy could at least take consolation from not having the worst round of the day, which belonged to Scotland's Robert MacIntyre, who shot a 12-over par 82.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On the Sky Sports Golf Podcast, Jamie Weir and Brad Faxon debate whether Rory McIlroy's extended break since The Open will help him win a record-extending fourth FedExCup title.

Memphis is hosting the first of three FedExCup Playoffs events, with only the top 50 in the overall season standings at the end of Sunday's final round progressing to the BMW Championship, and then the top 30 qualifying for the season-ending Tour Championship.

McIlroy's position of 12th out of the 70-player field means there is no concern about his progress to the BMW Championship, while the fact the events have no cut gives him plenty of time to climb the leaderboard over the weekend.

How do the FedExCup Playoffs work?

All season long, players have earned points based on how they have performed in PGA Tour events, with extra points available for the signature events and majors.

Only the top 70 in the standings have reached the FedEx St Jude Championship (August 13-16), with just the top 50 then progressing to the BMW Championship (August 20-23) and then only the top 30 making it to the finale, The Tour Championship (August 27-30).

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Brooks Koepka was extremely disappointed after failing to make the FedExCup playoffs.

Winners of the first two play-off events earn 750 points apiece - the same as The Players and the majors - before the points reset to zero ahead of the Tour Championship.

In the closing event, all players begin at even par, with the starting-strokes model based on FedExCup placings at that point axed in 2025.

The winner of the Tour Championship becomes FedExCup champion for 2026, earning $10m (£7.4m) and a five-year PGA Tour exemption.

Live coverage of the first event of the PGA Tour's FedExCup Playoffs, the FedEx St. Jude Championship, continues at 5pm on Friday. Watch live on Sky Sports Golf and Sky Sports Main Event or stream with no contract.

Sports.title: Leicester City up for sale for more than £200m
Sports.content:
Thai owners King Power are seeking to sell Leicester City for more than £200m.

The former Premier League champions engaged with Citibank to sound out potential buyers, it was reported last month.

Sky Sports News has now seen a sales pitch brochure produced by the investment bank, detailing the investment opportunity and the infrastructure which is included for sale at the club.

The dossier lists as up for sale: the men's and women's teams, King Power Stadium, both the women's and the men's training facilities, and OH Leuven, Leicester's sister club in Belgium.

The project is titled "Project Lineup" and values the physical assets at £224m with no specific sum placed on the sale of King Power's football teams.

In 2023, the club purchased the land around the King Power stadium for redevelopment, with plans to expand the capacity to 40,000, build a new hotel and entertainment complex.

Citigroup forecast the club's revenue during the 2026 financial year to be £97m.

However, the bank do not mention the club's two relegations between 2023 and 2025 and the financial losses that caused.

Image: Leicester City won the Premier League 10 years ago but are now in League One

King Power, run by the Srivaddhanaprabha family, bought Leicester for £35m from Milan Mandaric in 2010.

In recent years, King Power have converted a lot of debt into equity, to the tune of almost £300m. That has meant, apart from some small maintenance loans, the club is largely debt-free.

Sky Sports News has been told King Power have no urgency to sell, and they will continue to fund the club to the fullest until such time as a new, credible buyer steps forward. They have backed head coach Russell Martin this summer, with nine new signings.

The document states that Leicester is the sixth most successful team in English football since 2000, making this a "rare opportunity" to buy a club with a record of "winning promotions to higher divisions".

Image: Leicester City famously won the Premier League in 2015/16

As well as their surprise Premier League win in 2016, Leicester also won the FA Cup and Community Shield in 2021.

These successes are all included in the sales pitch, but their current position in League One is not referenced.

The document also cites Ben Chilwell, Harvey Barnes and Kieran Dewsbury-Hall as profitable recent transfers, with Gary Lineker and Emile Heskey listed at notable former players.

Sky Sports News contacted Leicester City for comment but they have declined to do so.

Analysis: 'Finding the right purchaser could take years'

Sky Sports News' Rob Dorsett:

"On the face of it, it seems bizarre that King Power would look to sell Leicester City at a time when the club is at its lowest ebb, and at one of its lowest market values, with the team in League One after three relegations in four seasons.

"But in truth Aiyawatt Srivaddhanaprabha has been seeking new investment for several years - all that is new here is the glossy brochure which advertises the club for sale, accentuating its assets. It is now being actively marketed for sale by financial specialists.

Image: Aiyawatt Srivaddhanaprabha holding the FA Cup

"That brochure - unusual as it is - is concrete evidence of a looming end of an era. King Power want out - having delivered unprecedented success in the form of the most unlikely of Premier League titles, an FA Cup, Champions League football and a Community Shield.

"For some Leicester fans, all that success has been tarnished by recent failures, and there have been protests against the ownership, and the director of football, Jon Rudkin. Serious mistakes have been made, for sure, in the management of the club in recent years, which has seen Leicester crash into League One, after boasting to be the club which came closest to breaking the "Big Six" Premier League monopoly over the last decade.

"But those dissenting Leicester fans should be careful what they wish for. On the open market, the football club is a very attractive prospect - almost entirely debt-free (thanks to the generosity of King Power in turning almost all of their £300m debt into equity in recent years) and with fully owned assets that are the envy of much bigger clubs in the Premier League. Their Seagrave training ground is a better facility than all but a handful of others in Europe.

"However, despite all their recent success, Leicester's fan-base is not as sizeable as many of the big clubs in the Championship, and having dropped into the third tier, even promotion at the first attempt would mean they didn't have the benefit of parachute payments in the second tier. All of those facts will be taken into account by would-be buyers.

"So don't expect a quick sale of the club. It could take years to find the right purchaser. The good news for Foxes fans is that King Power will not relinquish their responsibility as custodians, just because they have made the decision to sell. Nine new signings this summer is evidence of their determination to still support the football club. And the goodwill that the Thai business leaders still have for Leicester will almost certainly mean that they won't sell to the highest bidder, just to make a quick buck.

"Khun "Top" knows his legacy is at stake, and in memory of his late father, who died tragically in a helicopter crash in the stadium car park, he will no doubt want to sell the club to a new owner who can take the club forward, and once again make it a success."

Sports.title: Draper beaten in Cincinnati first round after blowing second-set lead
Sports.content:
Jack Draper lost 6-3 7-5 to Martin Landaluce in the first round of the Cincinnati Open after blowing six set-point chances to level the match.

Little more than a week on from a first-round defeat in Montreal on his return from injury, Draper was once more unable to maintain a consistent level as he succumbed to the Spaniard.

After being broken in the first game of the match on his way to losing the first set, Draper looked set to level when he went 5-2 up in the second having secured a double-break.

However, he would fail to take six set points spread across the next three games as Landaluce broke twice to level at 5-5.

Draper saved a match point for Landaluce before bringing up a chance of his own to force a tie break, but he was denied before his opponent closed out the match in just short of two hours.

The 24-year-old appeared extremely glum in the closing stages, but at least appeared to finish the match without any major fitness issues.

During his defeat to Terence Atmane in Montreal, the power of Draper's shots notably dropped off in the third set, while he was also in tears during the changeover.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jack Draper in tears on return from injury at the Canadian Open.

The circumstances in Montreal suggested Draper had reaggravated the left-arm injury that has plagued him since June 2025, at which point he had reached a career-high world ranking of fourth, but a swift return to the practice courts in Cincinnati calmed concern over his physical state.

While only Draper and his team know his true physical condition, it is clear that he is struggling to find anything like his best form, with the final major of the year - the US Open - starting in New York on August 30.

Sports.title: Doyle: Coppull can strike in the Hungerford
Sports.content:
Our ambassador previews four contests on Newbury's Hungerford Day and assesses the big races at Ripon - both cards live on Sky Sports Racing.

Extra furlong ideal for Hungerford fancy

Coppull showed me enough in the Group One July Cup to convince me he is up to taking the Visit Malta Hungerford Stakes (3.10) at Newbury on Saturday, live on Sky Sports Racing.

Clive Cox's three-year-old took a long time to get organised at Newmarket where the winner - Comanche Brave - got first run but this strong traveller should enjoy the extra furlong on a more conventional track.

Never So Brave will have his supporters on the back of his second in the Criterion at York over this seven-furlong trip but is struggling to get his head in front this season while Godolphin's Symbol Of Honour is solid but has never won over this distance.

A more interesting runner for me is William Haggas's Extremely Zain, a course and distance winner who ran better than his final placing suggests in the International at Ascot and remains on an upward curve. This is a step up in grade, but he can acquit himself well in an ordinary renewal.

Millionaire sets standard in Geoffrey Freer

Dubai Honour, who has four Group Ones and over £5 million in prize money on his CV, can roll back the years in the opening Highclere Thoroughbred Racing Geoffrey Freer Stakes (1.25) at Newbury.

This eight-year-old has given my husband Tom (Marquand) some of his finest moments in the saddle and, with an excellent record fresh, can make it win number 11 on his return from a summer break.

There is little between Mount Atlas and Tabletalk on their efforts in the Silver Cup at York, but I can't see either finding the improvement needed to lower the colours of Dubai Honour on these terms.

Gamrai went down fighting in the Copper Horse at Royal Ascot and, whilst he's in deeper waters now, may just benefit from the change of scenery, having joined George Scott from John and Thady Gosden.

Fire can burn it up in Sprint Handicap

Now he has got his head back in front, Richard Hannon's Wheels Of Fire can put up another bold show in the D&H, Excellence In Nutrition Handicap (1.55) at Newbury.

He beat the re-opposing Hypnotised comfortably at Sandown and a six-pound rise may not be enough to stop him following up under Pat Dobbs, even though that rival is better off at the weights.

Chris Mason's Glamorous Breeze is entitled to go close on her solid performance at Goodwood, but Kinswoman has come up short in Listed and Group company and still has something to prove, even though she's dropping back into a handicap off a reduced rating.

Humam set to build on Newmarket third

Humam's front-running third in a warm race at Newmarket puts him bang there for the TPT Fire Handicap (2.35) at Newbury. I loved the way this former Andrew Balding runner stuck to the task to register his best effort for Stuart Williams since being gelded in the winter.

Racing off an unchanged mark, his most recent form is more compelling than that of market rival Scoville, who has disappointed in both the Royal Hunt Cup and the Golden Mile at Goodwood and needs to improve for this drop in trip.

Eve Johnson Houghton's admirable Great Acclaim has been running well in big races such as the Victoria Cup and Buckingham Palace but needs some respite from the handicapper.

Roxby can initiate big-race double

Malton trainer Nigel Tinkler and his apprentice Alex Jary have a great chance of pulling off a memorable big race double at Ripon on Saturday, starting with Lord Roxby in the William Hill/MND Association Great St Wilfrid Handicap (3.25).

Middleham Park's four-year-old returns to the North Yorkshire track in top form after beating fancied rival Dark Cloud Rising over course and distance at the start of the month. He also put a big field to the sword at York earlier this summer and can cope with a five-pound rise against some smart rivals who have a bit more to prove.

Likely favourite Fast Track Harry put in an improved performance in first-time cheekpieces at Ascot last time but I'm not convinced the track will suit while the class horse in the race, Aramram, must overcome a low draw and he ran badly from a similar position in this race two years ago.

Boy can turn on the Magic in Silver Cup

In the consolation race, the William Hill Supporting MND Silver Cup Handicap (2.55), Nigel runs Magic Boy who ticks plenty of boxes in a wide open, big field dash.

This four-year-old is less exposed than most and showed his potential with a hard-fought win against 18 rivals at York last month before a slow start compromised his chances back there three weeks ago.

Magic Boy is ideally drawn in stall 14 and has previous track form which is always so important at the Garden Racecourse. He has finished second on both his visits but can go one better despite needing a career best.

Another interesting contender is Clive Cox's Mythical Composer who is also potentially well-drawn in stall 15 but needs to bounce back from a poor effort at Goodwood, his first since being gelded.

Hollie Doyle was speaking to Sky Sports Racing's Simon Mapletoft.

Sports.title: Celtic sign midfielder Baur on an initial four-year deal
Sports.content:
Celtic have made their fourth summer signing with midfielder Mika Baur joining on an initial four-year deal, with the option for a further year.

The 22-year-old arrives in a deal worth around £6.8m, joining from German club Paderborn, after helping them win promotion from the second tier of German football to the Bundesliga.

He scored four times and provided five assists across 33 league appearances last season, and was named the club's player of the year.

Sky Sports News understand the Scottish champions will pay an initial fee of around £4.5m for Baur, with £2.3m in add-ons making up the deal.

Similar to deals struck with fellow summer signings Camilo Duran, Kasper Høgh and Haissem Hassan, a large proportion of the bonuses will be paid out if Celtic reach the league phase of the Champions League.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Summer signing Kasper Hogh scored a hat-trick in just his second league game at Celtic

Celtic face LASK Linz in their play-off tie next week, and Baur - who came through the youth ranks at Freiburg before moving to Paderborn in 2024 - could now be registered for that Champions League squad.

On joining the Scottish Champions, Baur said: "It's absolutely the right move.

"It's a great club and I've heard incredible things about the fans.

"I'm in the same agency as Nicolas Kuhn so I called him to ask a couple of questions and he was so positive. He said, if you have the chance, just do it.

"I've had a good pre-season with good matches and tough training sessions, everything. So I'm in good shape and I'm ready to go."

Wolves v Blackburn, Friday 8pm, live on Sky Sports

Image: Wolves vs Blackburn

Wolves hold the tag of second favourites for the Championship title at 5/1 with Sky Bet - and rightly so - but I'm always wary of backing teams that have made losing football matches a habit, especially in the early stages of a season when playing a level down.

When assessing the last 10 teams that enter the Championship having taken 25 or points or less in the Premier League, their record across the first five games of the season is poor. Of those 50 games, the relegated team won just 15 - a strike rate of just 30 per cent.

The market has Wolves in at 1/2 here, meaning an implied probability of 66 per cent. That looks a shade too high for me, based on the unknowns still regarding this Wolves side. Also, those 50 games also produced a goals per game average of 2.1 which points towards this being a low-scoring fiddly opener for Wolves, who might be lacking some rhythm.

Tony Mowbray takes charge of Blackburn again and despite his health issues and below-par results at his last three clubs, his teams did only concede 1.1 expected goals per 90 minutes across that 85-game sample size. Under 2.5 goals at Evens with Sky Bet is the bet.

SCORE PREDICTION: 1-1 | JONES KNOWS' BEST BET: Under 2.5 goals (Evens with Sky Bet)

Bolton v Preston, Saturday 12.30pm, live on Sky Sports

Image: Bolton vs Preston

Preston had a very strong record away from home against the bottom half last season, losing just three of those 15 games but there was a big over-performance which averaged at 0.9 goals per game when you analyse the expected goals supremacy.

The departure of captain Ben Whiteman to Wrexham and the loss of important attacking contributions from Lewis Dobbin and Daniel Jebbison also give Paul Heckingbottom a problem. He saw his team lose four on the bounce in pre-season and a season of struggle could be on the cards.

Looking at previous seasons, newly-promoted teams in the Championship have a solid record of starting the season full of momentum and Bolton can land favourites backers a winner here at 5/4 with Sky Bet.

SCORE PREDICTION: 2-1

Bristol City v Millwall, Saturday 3pm, live on Sky Sports

There is a temptation to look at Millwall's third-place finish last season and think: that was a bit of a freak, wasn't it?

I don't think it was.

Millwall were third because they were really good at accumulating points.

They won 24 of their 46 league matches, lost only 11 and conceded just 49 goals. Alex Neil has brought a greater degree of tactical flexibility without taking away the characteristics you associate with Millwall. His teams are organised, competitive and pragmatic but there is more individual quality within this squad than we've seen from many previous Millwall sides.

This summer represents a more substantial attempt to change direction for Bristol City which makes them a difficult team to rate, but with such upheaval this looks a good time for Millwall to go there and do Millwall things. Away win at 17/10 with Sky Bet.

SCORE PREDICTION: 1-2

Sports.title: Richards to face Kalajdzic showdown on Fisher bill
Sports.content:
British former world title challenger Craig Richards will take on Radivoje Kalajdzic in a 10-round light heavyweight showdown, while Lee Cutler faces Louis Greene in a middleweight clash, on Zuffa Boxing's Johnny Fisher bill at London's Copper Box Arena.

Richards vs Kalajdzic will serve as the chief support bout to the 10-round heavyweight main event featuring Fisher at Zuffa Boxing 11 on September 26, live on Sky Sports.

An opponent for 'The Romford Bull' will be announced in the coming days.
