World.title: PM: Land joining Madise in race 'should make the election interesting'
World.content:
Ülle Madise is now backed by more than 60 MPs, but Prime Minister Kristen Michal (Reform) still believes TalTech rector Tiit Land will also enter Estonia's presidential race.

Michal said he supports Chancellor of Justice Ülle Madise and believes she would make a good president.

"We have one candidate with the support of about 60 MPs, and more signatures are gradually coming in," Michal said Thursday, calling it good news. "This means the presidential election has its first candidate eligible to be elected in the Riigikogu."

The prime minister said said parties are still in talks with Land, the rector of Tallinn University of Technology, and Mart Helme, the founder and deputy chair of the Conservative People's Party of Estonia (EKRE), but expects Land to be nominated.

"That should make the election rounds in the Riigikogu interesting," he added.

'I don't understand what's stopping them'

Minister of Education and Research and Eesti 200 chair Kristina Kallas said the political expectations surrounding the election do not reflect the constitutional system established for electing the president.

"The idea that Estonia's president is simply appointed or that this is a contest between top officials makes a mockery of our constitutional order," Kallas said, emphasizing that the president's role in Estonia as head of state isn't significant enough to require such a broad public mandate.

"The law provides for the president to be elected by the Riigikogu," she added. "We don't have nationwide campaigns, debates or public forums."

Kallas praised the work the Riigikogu has put into the process over the summer, noting that the process is less a traditional election and moreso an agreement on who will represent Estonia for the next five years.

Kristina Kallas (Eesti 200) and Margus Tsahkna (Eesti 200). Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

With more than 60 MPs agreeing by now that that should be Madise, Kallas urged other parties to skip any political games, show good statesmanship and join in her support.

"If the other parties say they have no reservations or fundamental ideological objections to Madise, I don't understand what's stopping them from supporting her," the Eesti 200 chair said. "Our job is to come together and elect a president."

She added that Madise's international standing and strong knowledge of the Constitution would make her well suited to the role.

'This isn't some game'

Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna (Eesti 200) said every MP in his party's parliamentary group has already signed in support of Madise. "Eesti 200 stands 100 behind what we've said," he said.

He urged parties to put aside political maneuvering connected to the 2027 Riigikogu elections and focus first on their responsibility to Estonia.

"This isn't some domestic political game where it's all fun and games and we take shots at one another," Tsahnka continued. "Look around you — we haven't seen geopolitical turmoil like this since the Soviet Union, and it affects our security as well. Never forget that independence cannot be taken for granted."

The Riigikogu will convene to elect the next president of Estonia on September 2, with candidates to be formally nominated August 21–24.

World.title: AirBaltic says it will continue flying from Tallinn
World.content:
The future of Latvian airline airBaltic is in the hands of its creditors, Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs said. Potential strategic investors are waiting for airBaltic to become viable and profitable. Under the new business plan approved on Wednesday, the airline will fly to fewer destinations but with higher frequency.

Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs stepped out for the first time from behind the wall of business‑secrecy surrounding airBaltic and admitted that the situation is very serious. According to Kulbergs, the state as the majority owner effectively lost control of the airline years ago, when €380 million worth of bonds were issued at an enormous 14.5 percent interest rate.

"No company can bear such a burden if no changes are made and no strategic plan is reviewed. They simply continued flying. The state is essentially no longer the owner — airBaltic is in the hands of lenders. Rights over the company were lost in 2024 when €380 million in bonds were issued," Kulbergs said.

Andris Kulbergs. Source: ERR

Now €225 million in bridge financing must be raised, using the bond collateral. The first bondholder meeting failed due to lack of quorum, and both the transport minister and airBaltic's leadership are now negotiating to ensure that the second meeting, planned for Monday, produces a result.

"The coming weeks are decisive. We will see whether bondholders support the chosen path and secure temporary financing, and whether the new business plan can attract new capital," Kulbergs said.

AirBaltic supervisory board vice‑chair Jurgis Sedlenieks confirmed to ERR that under the new business plan, the airline's main base will remain in Riga, and flights will continue from Tallinn and Vilnius. The number of aircraft will decrease and is expected to settle at around 40 in the future.

"The airline will reduce destinations, but flights to those that remain will operate several times a week. Some routes launched this summer from Tallinn — for example Tallinn–Vienna — will continue into winter. This shows that we are continuing in Estonia, which is a very important market for the company," Sedlenieks said.

According to the Latvian prime minister, strategic investors interested in airBaltic do exist, but they will not make a decision before the company's restructuring is complete.

"They are willing to continue negotiations once the company's strategy and issues related to lenders have been resolved," Kulbergs said.

The state cannot be the only party covering airBaltic's financial risks, even though it is one of Latvia's most important companies, the prime minister noted.

World.title: Wildlife expert: Rising bear numbers could increase risk of human attacks
World.content:
Estonia's bear population has grown for two decades, and one wildlife expert warns that new, tighter hunting limits could increase the risk of conflicts with people.

Recent court decisions have significantly restricted bear hunting in Estonia, and Peep Männil, a wildlife expert at the Environment Agency, expects the country's brown bear population to grow faster as a result.

That could mean more agricultural damage, greater impacts on other wildlife and more encounters with people, including potential attacks.

Estonia was home to about 1,100 brown bears as of fall 2025, according to agency estimates. The population has grown by an average of 5 percent a year over the past decade, with growth accelerating in recent years.

Männil explained that officials estimate bear numbers using sightings, particularly of females with cubs, rather than trying to count individual animals. More than 7,000 observations were recorded across Estonia last year, most by hunters and other wildlife enthusiasts using trail cameras.

The Environment Agency then maps and analyzes the resulting data, in the same approach used to estimate wolf, lynx and other wildlife populations.

No deadly attacks

While the abundance of sightings and trail-camera images can make it seem like there are suddenly far more bears in Estonia, Männil said bear numbers have actually been growing steadily for about 20 years already.

"The growth rate of the bear population will likely increase now, which is logical," he said, commenting on recently tightened hunting restrictions.

The expert said a growing bear population could lead to more crop damage as well as affect moose numbers, as bears prey heavily on moose calves in their first weeks of life.

"Studies in Sweden have found that the impact [on moose] can be quite significant," he added.

While the risk to people remains relatively low in Estonia, Männil warned that a larger bear population still also means a greater chance of dangerous encounters.

Seven bear attacks on people have been recorded in Estonia in the past 25 years. None were fatal, but three resulted in injuries, most recently in 2022. Four occurred during hunting situations, after the bear had been shot.

"That number is too small to draw any conclusions about an upward trend, but the likelihood of more such incidents will certainly increase," he said.

Simple safety tips

Männil explained that attacks here are generally defensive rather than predatory, and can occur when a person and bear unexpectedly encounter each other at close range. The possibility of an encounter, however, should not keep people out of the woods.

"It would be so unfortunate if people stopped foraging for mushrooms or spending time in nature because they're afraid there are too many bears," he said.

With risks rising as bear numbers grow, the agency expert stressed that careful wildlife management is increasingly important.

"One of the broader goals of hunting is to prevent these kinds of large swings in wildlife populations as much as possible," Männil said. "They're no good for the species themselves or for the balance between species."

While urban sightings do happen, encounters are more likely while hiking or foraging. A few simple tips shared by the Estonian Hunters' Society (EJS) can help keep you safe if you run into a brown bear in the wild.

World.title: Argo Ideon: The purpose of Russia's 'parliamentary elections' is to secure Kremlin power
World.content:
The parties participating in the political performance are cogs in a totalitarian system; real opposition in Russia has either been physically eliminated or driven into exile abroad, writes Argo Ideon.

With Russia's Duma "elections" scheduled for September 18–20, a little more than a month remains. Work is underway to ensure the numbers look presentable for the Kremlin. Vladimir Putin is conducting a propaganda tour in the country's east — an area out of reach of Ukrainian drone strikes — visiting Novosibirsk and even the Kuril Islands, which Russia seized from Japan. Meanwhile, courts are busy cleansing the ballot lists of opponents.

Many observers predict that after the elections, Russia will face a broad mobilization for the war in Ukraine — either fully public or somewhat concealed to reduce tension. Unfortunately, that is a more consequential event than any election result.

It is clear that Russia has long ceased to hold parliamentary elections in the Western democratic sense. Over the first quarter of this century, even the few remaining features resembling real elections have largely disappeared.

What remains is a political staging whose purpose is to fill the State Duma building in Moscow with loyal puppets competing to praise Vladimir Putin's imperial worldview. They also continue the conveyor belt of repressive laws that has characterized the current Duma.

Governance in Russia typically runs vertically. This means that a lower‑level boss — such as a mayor or regional governor — must ensure that goals set by the presidential administration are met: what voter turnout must be, how many votes certain parties must receive. And the votes appear. Those who fail are deemed ineffective leaders. Lower levels then bend over backwards to make sure everything proceeds as prescribed.

"What remains is a political staging whose purpose is to fill the State Duma building in Moscow with loyal puppets."

Since access to the elections is strictly limited from the candidacy stage onward, the disciplined voting process adds little from Moscow's perspective. But the system must still function, the gears must keep turning. Otherwise, spontaneous developments and "anarchy" might occur, and people could get the idea that anyone might be allowed to come to power.

The parties currently in the State Duma are cogs in this machinery — "cartel parties," to use Estonian political veteran Mart Helme's expression. If a voter for some reason does not want to vote for a United Russia candidate, they can choose the slightly more social‑branded A Just Russia, the Communist Party appealing to Soviet nostalgia, New People emphasizing small‑business interests, and others.

But when it is necessary to support the Kremlin on key issues — such as annexing a neighboring country's territory or killing Ukrainian civilians — these pocket parties all sing in the same choir, some more eagerly than others.

The fiercest competition in the Duma is among those who demand more effective destruction of Russia's enemies and settling scores with the opposing side. In the past, the radical‑patriotic role was mainly filled by the Liberal Democratic Party led by Vladimir Zhirinovsky. Now, with Vladimir Volfovich gone for several years, the LDPR is losing its accustomed niche.

All Russian party leaders beat the same drum, starting with United Russia chairman Dmitry Medvedev. His social media posts insulting Europe and the entire Western world have become a phenomenon of their own. In the early 2000s, Medvedev was still seen as representing the more liberal wing of the Russian elite, with a fondness for 1970s rock stars like Deep Purple and Black Sabbath…

Real opposition in Russia has been physically destroyed or driven abroad. Boris Nemtsov and Alexey Navalny — who were able to mobilize voters — have been killed. Much of the political emigration deemed "offenders" by the Russian state has been subjected to "civil death" under rules established by the Duma — they cannot use property in Russia or most state services.

Recently, the only party openly calling for peace in Ukraine, Yabloko, was banned from participating in the elections. But even among Russian émigrés, opinions differ on Yabloko's role.

One of Russia's best‑known dissidents, Vladimir Kara‑Murza, writes in The Washington Post that Yabloko became a channel through which Russian citizens could legally express opposition to the war in Ukraine, and the Kremlin grew afraid of them. "Putin panicked," Kara‑Murza argues.

Russian publicist Igor Eidman, living in Germany, instead says the authorities did not start fearing Yabloko; rather, developments in Russia's state system have reached a point where even symbolic or marginal dissent has no place.

"There is no longer any polyphony: all actors must speak with one voice, the same voice," Eidman writes on social media. "The state is returning to classic Stalinist‑type totalitarianism."

World.title: Paide out of UEFA Conference League after Rapid Vienna loss
World.content:
Eesti Meistriliiga side Paide Linnameeskond are out of the UEFA Conference League after losing their third-round qualifier second leg 2-0 away to Austrian legends Rapid Vienna.

Paide's route to the third-round qualifier saw them beat Lithuanian club Hegelmann 4-1 on aggregate, before overcoming Azerbaijani side Zira 2-1, also on aggregate.

However, a 4-1 defeat at home in the first leg last week had left Paide's chances almost hopeless, and they were unable to pull off a miracle on the road, exiting 6-1 on aggregate.

On Wednesday, Rapid forward Marco Tilio opened the scoring in the 37th minute, while Louis Schaub converted a penalty in the 82nd.

The 32-time Austrian Bundesliga winners enjoyed 65 percent of possession and saw as many as 23 shots, seven of them on target, compared with the visitors' two and one.

Rapid Vienna next face arguably an even bigger club, Portugal's Benfica, who similarly dispatched Scottish Premier League side Heart of Midlothian 6-1 on aggregate in their third-round qualifier.

World.title: Eesti Pank to issue Hiiumaa‑themed €2 coin
World.content:
The central motif of the coin is Hiiumaa's landmark, the Kõpu Lighthouse, surrounded by sea waves, with the light beams reflecting the striped pattern of Hiiumaa's traditional folk skirt. This pattern is an important part of the island's identity, symbolizing continuity and resilience, and representing the security of the home island.

The design is by Kaupo Kangro.

The Kõpu Lighthouse was completed in its original form in 1531 and is the third‑oldest operating lighthouse in the world.

One million coins dedicated to Hiiumaa will be minted and released into circulation through retail channels. The coin will be valid as official legal tender throughout the euro area.

Hiiumaa, known for its distinctive nature and long maritime history, will open Eesti Pank's new coin series dedicated to Estonia's counties. The aim of the series is to highlight the diversity and cultural uniqueness of Estonia's regions.

World.title: Economy minister rejects proposed restrictions on nicotine products
World.content:
Economy Minister Erkki Keldo declined to approve a draft bill aimed at curbing the use of nicotine products among young people as the proposed changes could have a significant impact on sellers and importers.

The restrictions proposed by the Ministry of Social Affairs and the Ministry of Justice would allow nicotine pouches, nicotine strips and nicotine sprays containing no more than four milligrams of nicotine per gram to be sold in Estonia. The aim is to reduce the use of nicotine products among young people.

Erkki Keldo sent a letter to the Ministry of Justice and Digital Affairs on Wednesday informing it that he had declined to approve the draft bill. Keldo said the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications supports protecting the health of children and young people and curbing the illegal sale of nicotine products, but considers it important that measures restricting freedom of enterprise be sufficiently justified and proportionate.

Snus. Source: Flickr

"The changes proposed in the draft bill could significantly affect manufacturers, importers, wholesalers and retailers of nicotine products operating in Estonia. The explanatory memorandum does not adequately assess the extent of these impacts or provide a convincing justification for the proposed maximum nicotine content of 4 mg/g for nicotine-containing products related to tobacco products," Keldo said.

He noted that the draft bill's maximum nicotine content of four milligrams per gram is based on Latvia's approach, but said this was not sufficient justification for restricting freedom of enterprise.

"The explanatory memorandum does not indicate the nicotine content of nicotine pouches and other products covered by the bill currently on the Estonian market, what proportion of products currently marketed legally would comply with the proposed limit or how many businesses and products would be affected by the change," the economy minister said.

He is also dissatisfied that the draft bill does not include a comparative analysis of approaches taken by other EU member states or explain why Latvia's regulations are the best model for Estonia.

Keldo said the explanatory memorandum needs to be supplemented with a comparison of different options. The impact of the limit on the health of children and young people, the risk of accidental poisoning, businesses, the functioning of the legal market and consumer behavior should also be analyzed.

The data presented in the explanatory memorandum concern products containing e-cigarette liquid, but does not address the impact of the changes on nicotine pouches, strips, sprays and heated nicotine sticks.

"We ask that the impact assessment be expanded to separately cover all product categories regulated by the draft bill and the requirements proposed for them," the minister said.

Keldo also wants the impact of the changes on Estonian manufacturers, exports, employment and regional businesses to be examined, along with their impact on the legal market, illegal trade and tax revenue.

"Possible substitution behavior must also be analyzed, including whether some consumers could switch to products with unregulated contents or to other tobacco and nicotine products and what impact this could have on achieving the draft bill's public health objective," Keldo said.

The Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications is also dissatisfied with a provision in the draft bill stipulating that products may not contain substances that produce a flavor or aroma other than tobacco or menthol and that only substances listed in a specific regulation may be used to provide those flavors. However, the explanatory memorandum does not explain why those particular substances are considered suitable or what costs businesses could incur in reformulating existing products.

Keldo said the bill's relationship with the planned update of the European Union's legal framework for tobacco and nicotine products should also be assessed.

The Ministry of Social Affairs has previously said that people are starting to use nicotine products at increasingly younger ages. While young people previously tried nicotine at ages 15 or 16, they are now doing so at around age 11. Nicotine pouches and e-cigarettes are the most common products used by those starting out.

Estonia's so-called Superministry building housing several government ministries. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

Just over one-fifth of the nicotine products currently on the market comply with the requirements proposed in the draft bill. Around 60 percent of products would have to be reformulated, while nearly one-fifth would have to be removed from the market.

Several European countries have tightened restrictions on nicotine products in recent years. Latvia raised the minimum age for purchasing tobacco and nicotine products to 20 two years ago. No such proposal is currently under consideration in Estonia.

The new rules are planned to take effect in 2028, although the exact date will be determined as the draft bill moves through the legislative process.

World.title: Baltics' first AI factory to open in Estonia
World.content:
Dutch cloud company Nebius' Tallinn AI factory will begin operating at Greenergy Data Centers' data center this year. With a capacity of 22 megawatts, it will be the largest in the Baltics.

Nasdaq-listed Nebius announced Wednesday that it signed agreements in the second quarter to expand the company's AI infrastructure network in Europe. The first phase of its Tallinn AI factory, with a capacity of 22 megawatts, is expected to begin operating later this year.

Nebius Head of Communications Tom Blackwell said Estonia was a natural choice for the company thanks to its world-class engineers, vibrant digital economy and startup culture, as well as its ambitious plans for both artificial intelligence and the transition to clean energy.

"Nebius' Tallinn AI factory, which is being developed in partnership with Greenergy Data Centers, will provide state-of-the-art infrastructure to support Estonia's growing innovation ecosystem and help accelerate the development and adoption of artificial intelligence," he said.

Nebius' global capacity network has expanded rapidly. In Europe, the company is developing large-scale AI factories in Lappeenranta, Finland, and Béthune, France. It also has an operating center in Mäntsälä, Finland, as well as AI infrastructure projects in the United Kingdom, Spain and Iceland. Nebius' major customers include Microsoft and Meta.

Greenergy Data Centers CEO Kert Evert said Nebius' decision to choose Greenergy shows that Estonia is emerging as a competitive destination for large-scale AI infrastructure projects.

Blackwell said Nebius wants to work closely with the Estonian government, businesses and universities to develop AI skills, broaden access to artificial intelligence capabilities and strengthen Estonia's position as a leading hub for AI innovation.

Martin Salo, co-founder of Tensor Estate, a group of Estonian entrepreneurs that became a shareholder in Greenergy Data Centers last month, said the newly announced project is the first phase of a larger development that will make Estonia one of the international hubs for AI infrastructure in the coming years.

"Until now, Northern Europe's major AI factories have been concentrated primarily in Finland, Sweden and Norway, thanks to favorable electricity prices, renewable energy and a suitable climate. Having the Baltics' first AI factory come here means Estonia is joining the club of countries where the world's leading AI companies are building their infrastructure," Salo said.

In late July, Greenergy Data Centers' Head of Hyperscale Martin Rungi told ERR that attracting one major international customer to Estonia would make it significantly easier for data centers to secure additional customers, as the market develops after the first breakthrough.

In Nebius' case, however, the question of its ties to Russian technology company Yandex cannot be overlooked, as Nebius emerged after Yandex came under sanctions following Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

In 2024, the company sold its Russian business units and changed its name to Nebius Group, which is headquartered in the Netherlands. Nebius CEO Arkady Volozh is also a co-founder of Yandex, but has since renounced his Russian citizenship.

A Greenergy representative said last month that such labeling was inappropriate, arguing that Nebius is probably one of the most thoroughly vetted organizations, given that despite its former ties to Russia, it has earned the trust of Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia, the U.S. government and the New York Stock Exchange.

Economy minister: We have consulted security agencies

As government agencies have had concerns about Nebius and the workforce at the AI factory set to operate in Hüüru, Estonian security agencies have been consulted, Minister of Economic Affairs and Industry Erkki Keldo said.

"On the one hand, cutting-edge investments like these /.../ are certainly very welcome in Estonia, but on the other hand, the government has an obligation to look at the broader security picture. So yes, we are aware of the background, we are also in contact with Estonian authorities and will certainly minimize the risks," he said, adding that it is very important to understand that the factory is purely a private investment.

If questions arise about a company's background or workforce, there are rules and security agencies in place, and those agencies have also informed the public about potential risks and threats, the minister noted.

"We certainly have to ensure that any sensitive data, sensitive sectors and sensitive technologies do not, for example, fall into the hands of high-risk countries. And when using different types of data, we have to pay attention to whose technology we are using and where we use and store data, to ensure that it is protected. That is certainly what we are doing," Keldo said.

According to Keldo, Nebius was also discussed at a Cabinet meeting on Thursday and discussions on the matter will continue in the coming weeks.

"Estonian businesses need to understand these potential risks, including the company itself and that people with Russian backgrounds and Russian contacts are not welcomed here with overly open arms. We are certainly somewhat more vigilant about this than perhaps other European countries are, and that will remain the case in the future," Keldo said.

The article was updated to add comments from Minister Erkki Keldo.

World.title: Baghdad and Erbil agree on unified digital customs system across Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Baghdad and Erbil have agreed to fully adopt the digital ASYCUDA customs system across border crossings, with non-oil border earnings shared equally by the federal and Kurdistan regional governments.

The deal is a significant step toward standardizing customs processes across Iraq and addressing long-standing disagreements over border revenues and claimed import quantities.

ASYCUDA, designed by the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD), digitizes customs declarations, payments, and clearing processes, allowing authorities to better monitor products entering the nation and the income they earn.

Linking customs operations to Iraq’s banking and electronic payment systems may help limit the potential for underreporting, revenue leakage, and corruption at border crossings.

The deal comes as Iraq’s Finance Ministry and Central Bank work to digitize customs, payments, and government financial data in collaboration with UNCTAD.

A combined computerized customs system for Baghdad and Erbil might give more accurate revenue data while resolving one of the two governments’ ongoing financial issues.

The change is also significant for Iraq’s overall economy.

More open and uniform customs processes might facilitate cross-border commerce, boost governmental revenues, and enhance the business climate as Iraq pursues more foreign investment and closer integration with international markets.

World.title: Iraq’s Chief Justice Faiq Zidan meets Syrian President Al-Sharaa in Damascus
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq’s Supreme Judicial Council President Faiq Zidan met with Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa in Damascus on Thursday, marking another high-level Iraqi outreach to a neighboring Arab state as Baghdad seeks to bolster regional relations under rising security problems.

Al-Sharaa welcomed Zidan and an Iraqi delegation to the People’s Palace, which also included Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani and Justice Minister Mazhar al-Wais.

According to the Syrian president, the talks focused on extending judicial and legal cooperation between Iraq and Syria, as well as resolving mutual concerns.

The visit also resulted in more practical conversations among the two nations’ judicial officials. Iraqi and Syrian authorities agreed to set up joint judicial committees to continue working on cases involving Syrian prisoners and other cross-border legal issues.

Zidan’s visit is crucial as he is one of the most prominent persons in Iraq’s state institutions, and it coincides with Baghdad’s increased diplomatic, security, and judicial interaction with its neighbors.

The Damascus meetings come after a separate Iraqi security group visited Riyadh, where senior military official Abdul Amir al-Shammari met with Saudi Defense Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman.

Zidan had also just visited Ankara as part of a larger Iraqi effort to build ties with Saudi Arabia, Syria, and Turkey.

That approach has become more urgent in light of the regional escalation involving Iran-backed Iraqi forces.

In late July, the United States and Saudi Arabia conducted synchronized attacks against locations used by Iran-aligned organizations in Iraq, after Riyadh accused militias operating from Iraqi territory of firing drones against Saudi energy infrastructure.

The incident put Baghdad under strong pressure to prevent armed organizations from exploiting Iraqi territory to launch assaults on neighboring nations and also highlighted the potential that militia activity may harm Iraq’s improved ties with Arab governments.

Against this setting, Zidan’s encounter with Al-Sharaa is significant beyond regular court cooperation.

Iraq and Syria share a long border and confront shared concerns such as terrorism, organized crime, prisoners, and cross-border security. Baghdad also has a strategic interest in preserving stable ties with Damascus, as Iraq strives to boost regional connections and prevent unrest from spilling over its borders.

Iraq’s Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi’s administration sees recent diplomatic efforts as part of a larger effort to strengthen Iraq’s ties with its neighbors while keeping the nation out of the developing conflict between Iran and its regional adversaries.

Baghdad has increasingly emphasized that choices on security, armament, and relations with neighboring governments must be made by Iraqi official authorities rather than armed groupings.

The travels to Damascus and Riyadh therefore convey an essential message: although Iran-aligned militias have exacerbated tensions between Iraq and certain of its neighbors, Iraqi official institutions are working directly with those nations to restore cooperation and avoid further escalation.

Strengthening judicial, diplomatic, and security ties with Syria, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey might serve as an essential regional buffer for Iraq as it seeks to safeguard its sovereignty, control armed groups, and avoid being drawn further into the region’s crises.

World.title: Iraq’s Al-Shammari visits Riyadh to meet Saudi Defense Minister
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — A top Iraqi security team has traveled to Riyadh for meetings with Saudi Arabia’s leadership, as Baghdad and the Kingdom work to improve security and military cooperation after weeks of heightened tensions in Iraq involving Iran-backed militias.

First Lieutenant General Abdul Amir Al-Shammari, director of the Office of the Commander-in-Chief of the Iraqi Armed Forces, met with Saudi Defense Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman on Thursday to discuss military cooperation, regional developments, and increased coordination between the two nations.

According to reports from the visit, the conversations included cross-border drone concerns, air defense, and intelligence collaboration.

The conference is especially significant in light of the combined US-Saudi attacks on Iran-linked militia locations in Iraq on July 29.

Washington and Riyadh said the operation targeted Iran-backed terrorists’ weapons and logistical facilities in response to a series of drone assaults on Saudi oil installations that they said originated in Iraqi territory.

The strikes drastically escalated tensions between Baghdad and Riyadh, highlighting the Iraqi government’s problems in preventing armed groups from exploiting its territory to target neighboring nations.

Thursday’s visit indicates that both parties are now attempting to move beyond that conflict via direct military and intelligence collaboration.

Prince Khalid underlined Saudi Arabia’s commitment to Iraq’s security, stability, and economic growth, identifying it as an essential neighbor with whom the Kingdom has strong political and social relations.

The meetings in Riyadh follow Saudi intelligence head Khalid bin Ali al-Humaidan’s visit to Baghdad last week, during which he met with Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and reiterated an offer for the Iraqi leader to visit Saudi Arabia.

Baghdad’s security cooperation with Riyadh has grown more vital as the government seeks to prevent Iran-backed militias from drawing Iraq into a larger regional conflict.

Al-Zaidi has frequently said that Iraqi soil should not be used to attack other nations and has stepped up efforts for weaponry to be put solely under state control.

The most recent Iraqi trip to Riyadh symbolizes more than just normal defense diplomacy. It is part of a joint effort by Baghdad and Saudi Arabia to restore security trust after the July escalation and prevent militia activities from dragging the two neighboring nations into conflict.

World.title: Rare blind fish found in underground river in Iraq’s Anbar desert
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi security and environmental teams have discovered a fascinating underground water system deep under the dry Anbar desert, where rare eyeless fish thrive in total darkness.

The location is in the Al-Khasfa region near Haditha, and crews traveled through a remote desert cave and sinkhole system to access running groundwater hundreds of meters under the surface.

The expedition’s footage shows little, pale fish moving in the subterranean water in the lack of sunshine.

The fish have evolved to live in darkness by losing their eyes and pigmentation, giving them a characteristic white-to-pink look.

The crew traveled more than 500 meters into the cave system despite challenging terrain and low oxygen levels.

The difference between above- and underground has piqued interest: underneath what seems to be an isolated and very arid stretch of western Iraqi desert, there is flowing freshwater and a specialized ecology.

Initial investigations have also suggested a link between the subterranean water system and the Euphrates basin, with the watercourse possibly running for a long distance under the desert.

However, environmental experts have highlighted that the blind fish themselves are not a novel finding.

Qais Najeh, the chairman of the Anbar Environment Directorate, stated that experts first confirmed the occurrence of eyeless fish in Al-Khasfa in 2010.

Similar fish have also been discovered in subterranean water near the Sheik Hadid mausoleum in Haditha district.

According to experts, the fish may grow to be roughly 49 millimeters long and survive in rather steady groundwater temperatures ranging from 20 to 22 degrees Celsius.

Their lack of vision and pigmentation are adaptations to generations of living in perpetually dark subterranean habitats.

The recent mission is nonetheless noteworthy because it has refocused attention on one of Iraq’s least-known natural ecosystems, perhaps allowing scientists to better research the subterranean water network, its geology, and the creatures that rely on it.

The fish’s severely limited environment renders it vulnerable.

Changes in groundwater levels, pollution, or human intervention might endanger a population that has acclimated to highly particular subsurface circumstances.

The Al-Khasfa location offers a unique dimension to Anbar, a region best known for its wide western desert and the Euphrates.

Hidden under that terrain lies an environment few Iraqis have ever seen: flowing subterranean water that feeds fish who have evolved to survive their entire lives without sunshine.

World.title: Israel reopens once-closed West Bank settlement
World.content:
GANIM – Israel officially reopened the West Bank settlement of Ganim on Thursday, more than 20 years after it withdrew from the community, in a move emblematic of the current government’s policy of rapid settlement expansion.

The smell of freshly-poured asphalt hung in the air above Ganim’s new and only street, where future residents and their families — who had come to help with the move — smiled at the sight of their pre-fabricated homes.

“A month ago there was nothing here. A rocky mountain, barely any trees, barely any shade. We’re arriving now,” new resident Reut Baran, 35, told AFP in front of her new home.

In a nearby truck, dozens of brand new air conditioning units still in their boxes were waiting to be installed.

Matan Berkovitch, a 25-year-old who moved into the new settlement with his wife and child, said he was satisfied with the government’s policy towards settlements as he looked around a brand new home just connected to the electric grid.

“I’m happy to be part of a time like this where there are ministers in the government who support and guide us in the right direction and know how to get things done properly,” he said.

Berkovitch’s mother Carmit, who came from Jerusalem to move him in, said another one of her sons would soon study at the religious school in the settlement, and expressed pride at their active part in the settler movement.

“Here, this is the Land of Israel. Here, we are staying forever,” Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz said at the ceremony, after arriving by helicopter.

Ganim is one of four Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank that Israel evacuated under former prime minister Ariel Sharon’s disengagement plan in 2005.

The move came partly because of their isolated location in the north of the territory among many Palestinian cities and villages.

Under Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government, settlement construction and expansion have soared, including with the official re-establishment of three of the four evacuated communities — Ganim, Sa-Nur and Homesh.

In Ganim, about two dozen pre-fabricated homes have already been installed, while steamrollers and other construction machinery busily created new space for future houses on the hillside on Thursday.

About a hundred people from Israel and other West Bank settlements attended the ceremony, including Katz and Yossi Dagan, head of the Israeli authority in charge of settlements in the northern West Bank.

“The era of evacuation is over — from here, we only build,” Dagan said.

In the valley below, Palestinians who spoke to AFP feared Ganim’s construction would make their lives harder, or even mean eventual displacement.

On both sides of the road leading to the settlement from Israel, the army has demolished stores in recent days and blocked several dirt roads to Palestinian communities with piles of rubble.

Israel has occupied the West Bank since 1967. More than 500,000 Israelis live in settlements in the territory, which are illegal under international law, among some three million Palestinians.

Violence against Palestinians by Israeli settlers has increased dramatically since the October 7, 2023 attack on Israel by Hamas from the Gaza Strip.

World.title: Carrick urges Man Utd to push for more signings to boost title bid
World.content:
London – Michael Carrick has urged Manchester United to splash the cash to keep pace with their Premier League title rivals.

United have spent around £85 million ($114 million) on Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Karl Darlow since the end of last season.

But that outlay pales in comparison to some of United’s fellow title contenders, with Manchester City, Arsenal and Chelsea all paying huge fees for high-profile signings.

Carrick knows United need more quality and depth if they are to challenge for a first English title since 2013, while also competing in the Champions League.

Remarkably, United have never spent more than £89.5 million on a single player — the fee paid for Paul Pogba in 2016.

And ahead of his first season as permanent United boss after a successful interim spell last term, Carrick called on the club’s hierarchy to push for more new recruits.

“I think we’ve done really good business and we’ve got really some top, top, top players,” Carrick told reporters on Thursday.

“We’re delighted with that. We always want to improve. We want more, we need more, we keep looking for how we can do that. That never stops.”

Carrick led United to a third-place finish in the Premier League after he replaced the sacked Ruben Amorim.

But with United so far spending less than promoted sides Coventry and Ipswich, some fans are becoming restless as their Premier League opener at Hull on August 22 looms into view.

“Money’s money, I get that. It’s still about the football, and that’s where the competition lies,” Carrick said.

“Certainly the situation is what it is as well, whether that’s finances or whatever. For now, we’ve got to make the most of it, but we’ve got to keep pushing and push everything and every boundary that we can to be able to win again.”

Asked why United were not spending on the level of other clubs, Carrick added: “To be honest, I haven’t got the answers for that. We’re working with pushing everything that we can to make the best of it.”

Having spent last season on loan with Barcelona, Marcus Rashford is back at United this week after returning from the World Cup.

Barcelona declined their option to buy the 28-year-old England forward and questions remain over his United future.

“He’s our player, and he’s a good player and he gives us something a little bit different in the group,” he said.

“Marcus can offer us so much. He has done, and he can do again, so in that respect it’s quite exciting.”

Several United players have backed the team to dethrone Arsenal as champions and the understated Carrick wouldn’t rule out a title push.

“We’ve definitely got the potential to achieve something really special,” he said.

“I’m not hiding from the fact, and we should aim to do that, but I can’t give you a definite answer on that.

“It’s certainly what we’re pushing to do because we have to, because that’s the club we are.”

World.title: Leicester’s Thai owners put troubled club up for sale: reports
World.content:
London – Former Premier League champions Leicester have been put up for sale by the club’s Thai owners, according to reports on Thursday.

Just 10 years after their fairytale Premier League title triumph, Leicester will play in English football’s third tier for only the second time in their history this season.

The Foxes, who won their first FA Cup in 2021, have endured a dire period featuring successive relegations from the Premier League in 2025 and the Championship in 2026.

Last season, they were docked six points after breaching the Football League’s profit and sustainability rules, sparking their slump into League One.

A BBC report on Thursday said Leicester’s Thai owners King Power — run by the Srivaddhanaprabha family — have commissioned a leading US investment bank to help find a buyer, with the club’s assets said to be listed at more than £200 million ($269 million).

King Power bought Leicester in a £35 million deal in 2010.

Aiyawatt Srivaddhanaprabha took over as Leicester chairman following the death of his father Vichai in a helicopter crash outside the club’s King Power stadium in 2019.

Following last season’s relegation, Aiyawatt said he should shoulder the “blame” for the club’s predicament but also stressed the “structure will change”.

Russell Martin’s side kick off their promotion bid with a trip to Notts County on Saturday.

World.title: Iraq sets September 30 for US-led coalition exit as Al-Zaidi turns focus to Iran-linked militia weapons
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has reaffirmed Sept. 30 as the end date for the US-led coalition’s military mission in Iraq, putting more pressure on Baghdad to confront what could be the most difficult aspect of its sovereignty agenda: bringing weapons held by powerful Iran-aligned factions under state control.

During a meeting with U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) Commander Admiral Brad Cooper, Al-Zaidi said that October 1 will signal the beginning of a “new phase” for Iraq in the absence of a foreign coalition military presence.

The Prime Minister again emphasized the importance of the Iraqi state having exclusive control over weaponry, citing sovereignty, security, and economic growth.

Iraqi authorities said plans are already beginning to hand over remaining coalition locations, notably those in northern Iraq, to Iraqi security forces before the deadline.

The timeline is based on a 2024 agreement between Baghdad and Washington to end the coalition mission and transition the US-Iraq security partnership to direct bilateral cooperation.

However, the departure eliminates one of the primary justifications used by Iran-backed militias to preserve their weapons and strike US objectives.

Several prominent Iran-aligned factions work inside or alongside the Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), who are officially part of Iraq’s governmental security system.

The PMF is made up of various groups with varying political and ideological perspectives, and it should not be viewed as a unified bloc.

However, organizations like Kataib Hezbollah, Harakat al-Nujaba, and other Iran-aligned militias have maintained strong ties with Tehran and have rejected calls to relinquish their weapons.

Their actions have become an increasingly severe issue for Al-Zaidi’s administration.

Recent strikes ascribed by neighboring governments to Iran-backed forces operating from Iraqi soil have jeopardized Baghdad’s improved ties with Saudi Arabia and other Arab countries, as well as led to foreign military intervention in Iraq.

The escalation has put Baghdad in a difficult position: denouncing breaches of Iraqi sovereignty while also facing demands from its neighbors to prohibit armed groups from exploiting Iraqi territory to threaten them.

For Al-Zaidi, the September 30 withdrawal may fundamentally alter that equation.

Once the coalition mission is over, Iran-aligned elements will find it more difficult to justify maintaining autonomous military capabilities by citing the presence of foreign soldiers.

Baghdad will then have to decide whether it can impose its notion of a single armed authority in Iraq.

That problem is especially critical since Al-Zaidi is aiming to shift Iraq’s focus from decades of war and proxy conflict to rebuilding, investment, and closer economic ties with the US, Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Jordan, and other foreign allies.

Repeated militia assaults risk undercutting that plan by raising investor anxiety and subjecting Iraq to reprisal for military choices that its government claims were not authorized.

The coalition’s exit therefore means more than just the removal of foreign troops.

It might serve as the catalyst for a far wider debate over who eventually controls Iraq’s armaments and war-making choices.

Baghdad will find it easy to declare complete sovereignty on October 1.

Demonstrating it will be far more difficult.

If Al-Zaidi is serious about guaranteeing that no foreign military presence stays in Iraq, the same sovereignty concept will increasingly be expected to apply to armed forces whose allegiance, weapons, or choices are not under the control of the Iraqi state.

Bringing such weapons under state control might prove to be one of the most important—and difficult—tests of Al-Zaidi’s leadership.

A native of Marhama, Bijbehara, in south Kashmirâs Anantnag district, Sheikh went underground after the April 2, 1991, attack along with two co-accused even as their accomplice, Aman Ullah Khan, was caught that day. Charged under relevant provisions of the stringent Terrorist and Disruptive Activities (Prevention) Act, Explosive Substances Act, and Ranbir Penal Code, Sheikh managed to evade arrest for three-and-a-half decades by concealing his identity and assuming another, a GRP spokesperson said.

World.title: CAG finds 98% shortfall in Green India Mission forest cover targets, red-flags multiple lapses
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Red-flagging lapses in the countryâs ongoing programme to increase and improve green cover, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) has pointed out non-achievement of forest cover targets, noting that the observed increase in forest cover fell short by nearly 98% during 10 years of implementation (2015-16 to 2024-25) of the Green India Mission (GIM).

Releasing the performance audit report on the Mission, CAG highlighted the wrong choice of landscape for planting trees, absence of convergence of various schemes to increase green cover, financial mismanagement, improper planning, lack of coordination and deficient monitoring behind non-achievement of the GIMâs goals.

The broad objectives under the Mission were to increase forest/tree cover, improve the quality of forest/non-forest lands, improve ecosystem services, including biodiversity, hydrological services and carbon sequestration because of forest land/non-forest land, and to increase forest-based livelihood income of households living in and around forests.

Underlining its key audit findings, the CAG in its report tabled in Parliament on Wednesday said, âAs against the target of 1.4 million hectares (mha), improvement of forest cover quality was observed in only 0.11 mha (nearly 92% shortfall). Similarly, an increase in forest cover was observed in only 0.03 mha as against the target of 1.4 mha (nearly 98% shortfall).â

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

It also noted that despite vulnerability being a key criterion, landscapes with low to moderate priority were selected over those more vulnerable to climate change for afforestation under the Mission.





The performance audit examined the planning, implementation and monitoring of the GIM interventions in 16 states and UTs for which physical and financial targets were approved by the environment ministry during the period 2015-16 to 2024-25.

Pointing out deficient monitoring, the CAG noted that 14 states even failed to provide required public web links for transparency. It flagged that audit evaluations revealed inflated data and overstated achievements, and GIS analysis showed that 70% of sampled sites had no noticeable changes attributable to GIM.

World.title: 'Majority of students innocent': BCI reverses ban on NALSAR 2026 batch over CJI invite row
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Bar Council of India (BCI) on Thursday modified its controversial circular that had effectively barred graduates of Hyderabad's NALSAR University of Law's 2026 batch from enrolling as advocates.

In a fresh communication, released hours after the original decision, the BCI clarified that 2026 graduates of the university would be "entitled to seek enrolment with any state bar council of their choice".

"After thorough discussion, the members are of the unanimous view that as per the latest report, vast majority of the students of NALSAR (2026 pass out students) are innocent and they were not inclined to take part in the move of disrespect," the BCI statement said.

"It has further been reported by some reliable sources that a handful of teachers and outsiders were instrumental in instigating the inncoent student," the BCI said.

"No student shall be made to suffer without any fault on his part," it added.

The latest development came hours after the legal regulator triggered widespread criticism by directing all state bar councils not to enrol any student graduating from NALSAR in 2026 until further orders.





The earlier circular was issued after a section of graduating students at the premier law university objected to a reported proposal to invite Chief Justice of India Surya Kant as the chief guest at the institution's convocation.

"No student who has obtained a law degree from NALSAR University of Law in the year 2026 shall be enrolled as an advocate until further directions are issued by the Bar Council of India," the order had said.

The regulator had also sought a detailed report from the university within three days, asking it to identify students who had allegedly initiated, organised or mobilised the campaign against the proposed participation of the Chief Justice.

In a strongly-worded statement, BCI chairperson Manan Kumar Mishra had said students who did not show respect for the country's highest judicial office could not be expected to become responsible members of the legal profession.

"Such persons shall always be a liability on the profession. Such conduct reflects adversely upon the person's suitability for entry into or association with the legal profession and is inconsistent with the dignity, discipline and ethical standards of the legal profession," it added.

World.title: 'No clear information': Nepal ‘loses’ papers of centuries-old treaty defining borders with India
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Nepal has apparently lost the decades-old original of the 1816 Treaty of Sugauli, a document that largely defined the Himalayan nation's boundaries with British India, its foreign minister Shisir Khanal told Parliament on Monday.

Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal told the House of Representatives recently that while some treaty-related documents are held in the National Archives, their status as the original official documents remains unclear.

âThe Government of Nepal does not have clear information on whether we possess the official treaty documents. There are records showing that some documents related to certain treaties are kept at the National Archives.

But we do not have clear information as to whether those are the actual official treaties,â Khanal said.

He said Nepal does have documents related to the 1816 Sugauli Treaty and the 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship with India.

The disclosure comes amid renewed tensions over the Nepal-India border after India and China agreed to reopen the Lipulekh trade route. Nepal claims Lipulekh, Limpiyadhura and Kalapani as its territories, while India maintains that they are part of its territory.





This becomes significant, as the dispute resurfaced recently after Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah said Kathmandu had raised with India concerns over alleged encroachment, including in Lipulekh. Shah said both sides had agreed to examine the issue through historians, surveyors and territorial experts and resolve it through diplomatic talks. He also called for the UK to be involved, citing its role in shaping the region's borders during the colonial era.

Shah said Nepal had found that ânot only had India encroached on Nepal's land, but Nepal had also encroached on India's land in multiple places.â

India rejected any role for third parties, with MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal having said âthere is no role for any third parties in a bilateral matter between India and Nepal.â He said nearly 98% of the boundary had been demarcated, with remaining issues including stretches affected by the shifting Gandak River and cross-border occupation or encroachment on no-man's land.

India has also rejected Nepal's claims over Lipulekh, Kalapani and Limpiyadhura as âneither justified nor based on historical facts and evidence.

â

The issue of missing treaty documents has been around for years. In 2016, when the Eminent Personsâ Group on Nepal-India Relations began discussions on reviewing or replacing the 1950 treaty, Nepal tried to locate the original but failed to find it. The government subsequently provided the Bhekh Bahadur Thapa-led committee with another copy of the treaty.

The matter later prompted a parliamentary inquiry. On July 22, the Delegated Legislation and Governance Committee of Nepal's National Assembly concluded that the original copies of both the Sugauli Treaty and the 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship could not be found in the country.

The committee said it searched various locations where historical records could have been preserved, including libraries, archives and government repositories, as well as the Department of Archaeology, Narayanhiti Palace Museum, Ministry of Law and Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

The matter had also come up in Parliament in 2019. Then Foreign Minister Pradeep Gyawali said the government had copies of both treaties but was unsure whether they were originals. âWe have both treaties, but we have to forensically verify whether these copies are originals or not,â Gyawali had said. âWe are also trying to find historical documents and maps in India and the United Kingdom.â

Khanal's remarks came as he outlined a broader plan to review Nepal's existing international agreements.

He said the country has 655 treaties and agreements, including 412 bilateral and 243 multilateral agreements.

Of these, 55 have already been concluded or amended, while the government plans to review the remaining 600 based on their necessity and relevance. Khanal said older or inactive agreements would be reviewed, amended or renewed in coordination with the countries or international organisations concerned.

âUnder the general principles of international treaty law, the review, amendment, or renewal of any bilateral or multilateral treaty or agreement depends on the mutual consent and approval of the concerned state parties or relevant international organisations,â Khanal said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

He added that the government would undertake the exercise with the cooperation and approval of the relevant countries and international organisations.

What is the Sugauli Treaty?

The Sugauli Treaty was agreed between Nepal and the British East India Company after the Anglo-Nepalese War. It was signed in December 1815 and ratified in March 1816, with the agreement establishing the basis for Nepal's territorial boundary with British India.

The treaty required Nepal to cede significant territories to the East India Company and renounce claims to lands west of the Kali River, while also setting out provisions governing relations between Nepal and the Company.

World.title: From erotic fantasy to Indian identity, a famous Italian calendar finds a new story
World.content:
In 1966, a photograph of a woman in underwear arrived at the Vatican. The fashion imagery might seem rather tame by today's standards, but it was enough to provoke an official complaint from the Holy See to an Italian tire company called Pirelli.

The Milan-based tire manufacturer had just begun producing these exclusive, high-fashion calendars, simply called 'The Cal', as a trade gift for its top clients â the idea being to give VIPs something a cut above the cheap pin-up calendars that were standard fare in garages and tire shops at the time.

But the condemnation had the opposite effect. Rather than suppressing the calendar, it generated enormous publicity, transforming a niche corporate giveaway into one of the world's most coveted cultural status symbols.

Within a few years, the calendar became less a marketing gimmick and more an annual referendum on where European ideas of beauty, sex and provocation stood. Over the decades, figures from Naomi Campbell, Cindy Crawford and Kate Moss to PenÃ©lope Cruz, Serena Williams and Yoko Ono have been framed within its pages by some of the world's most influential photographers.

But sixty-two years and a great many controversies later, the most recent edition of that same calendar is shot not on a Mediterranean beach or a Manhattan studio, but in the forts and villages of Rajasthan and the mean streets of Old Delhi, even featuring everyday barbers and artisans.





The 2027 Pirelli Calendar is dedicated to India. For the first time, it features an all-India cast and is shot entirely in the country, built around the idea of Indian identity. So alongside glamorous portraits of celebrities like television host and author Padma Lakshmi, actress Aditi Rao Hydari, sitarist Anoushka Shankar and supermodel Bhavitha Mandava are some 200 ordinary Indians, from dancers and street artists to musicians and craftspeople.

One half of the 2027 Pirelli Calendar features Indian celebrities photographed by Norwegian photographer SÃ¸lve SundsbÃ¸ I Picture credit: Alessandro Scotti

The project began as a collaboration between Norwegian photographer SÃ¸lve SundsbÃ¸ and Raghu Rai, modern India's most celebrated photojournalist known for chronicling the country's many faces and contradictions over several decades. Rai died in April shortly after the project began. His daughter, photographer Avani Rai, stepped in to complete it and in doing so changed its direction. What had been conceived as a studio shoot moved outdoors into the neighbourhoods her father spent his career documenting, from Kinari Bazar and Yamuna Ghat to the streets of Old Delhi.

When asked how a project like the Pirelli Calendar sits alongside her reportage-driven practice, Avani, speaking to TOI, gently rejects the premise of the question. Genre, she argues, describes where a photograph ends up, not how it is made. What remains constant, whether in documentary work or a fashion commission, is the attempt to stay honest to what is in front of the camera. "Curiosity, presence and empathy are not specific to one genre of photography.

The Pirelli Calendar asked me to bring those values into a different context. I wasnât interested in making images that simply looked beautiful. I wanted them to feel alive. To hold the same emotional honesty that I search for in every photograph I make," says Avani whose mother, conservation architect Gurmeet Rai, also appears in the calendar.

Even to this day, The Cal's physical copies are not sold publicly; Pirelli limits production to roughly 20,000 copies annually and they are sent as corporate gifts to monarchs, CEOs, prime ministers, top celebrities, fashion icons and the like.

But why India? SundsbÃ¸ says it was a long-held ambition within Pirelli. His contribution came from a very different vantage pointâthat of an outsider conscious of his own limitations. "The fact that Avani and Raghu Raiâs images would be one half of the Calendar enabled me to concentrate on portraits. That's a smaller and more realistic task for a visitor than capturing the whole soul of a nation.I didnât try to decide what âIndiannessâ should mean.

Especially not as the guest that I am. I tried to cast people I admire, women who have inspirational talent," says SundsbÃ¸.

The edition also marks the first time Pirelli has commissioned two photographers to share a calendar. What makes the India edition notable is not simply that it swaps eroticism for cultural identity; the calendar has been moving in that direction for years. Rather, it is the first edition shaped by two intertwined perspectives: an outsider looking in and a daughter completing her father's final project in the streets he loved.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"I used to think inheritance was about continuing someoneâs work. Now I think itâs about continuing their way of being in the world. The patience they lived with. The integrity they carried. The generosity with which they met people. Those are the things that survive," says Avani.

"Completing the calendar gave me a sense of continuity. It wasnât about recreating him or holding onto the past. I understood that what he had really left me wasnât an archive or even a body of work. It was a practice of being alive to the world," she adds.

World.title: International location, multiple mule accounts and a physical property sale: police report on hybrid digital arrest scam in Delhi HC
World.content:
The Delhi Police submitted its status report in the High Court in the case pertaining to a hybrid digital arrest scam where an elderly woman was forced to sell her property in south Delhi and pawn her jewellery while under digital arrest. The woman had approached the High Court for a transfer of the case to Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) citing it as one of the ‘evolving’ cases due to its hybrid nature.

The counsel for the victim represented by Kush Sharma argued that the hybrid nature of the crime makes it the first documented case in India where a physical syndicate was operating during an active digital arrest. “The police report shows that the syndicate operated through a decentralised structure with separate groups responsible for victim communication, mule account holders’ recruitment and laundering of funds. The complexity of this hybrid crime makes it appropriate for CBI jurisdiction,” said Kush Sharma.

The police investigation as per status report revealed monetary transactions running into multiple layers with over ten bank accounts connected with first and second layer beneficiaries. The police tracked a phone number used to contact Sushant having an IP address based in Cambodia. The status report mentioned that the police have sent notices to account holders and are awaiting account holders’ details for some accounts.

A person named Nannu Singh, allegedly received funds as part of these transactions for his organization named ‘Savitri Bai Fule Education Welfare Society’, the report mentioned. He met at least six people who allegedly promised him to help ‘raise funds’ but disappeared after a transaction worth Rs 1 crore had been made with his account. The group was allegedly involved in buying of SIM cards and stayed at multiple hotels during the period of the scam, the report said.

The report further stated that Sushant had also received a call from a person named Nitin, claiming to be the victim’s son regarding the sale of property. Sushant told the police as mentioned in the report that he had facilitated the property deal taking the caller to be victim’s son and said that when he got to know that the victim had fallen prey to a digital scam, accompanied her to the police station for filing a complaint.

“The report however does not mention what did Sushant do with the money taken from the victim, which was first credited to her account but then withdrawn the very next day. It is clear that the syndicate had been functioning at both digital and physical level,” Kush said.

He also said that the CBI response did not come on record despite the court sending notices to them in the last hearing for submission of a response. “CBI report said that they have a threshold of Rs 10 crore and they don’t take cases for amount below that but we have argued that the case is exceptional and requires CBI jurisdiction due to its complexity,” he added.

The matter will next be heard on August 27.

Case Background

The incident took place in April this year when a 75-year-old woman living alone received a call from an unknown number wherein persons impersonating CBI told her she was found to be a part of a money laundering case and she had to deposit all her money and property with them or else her children living abroad would be expatriated back to India.

As she transferred over Rs three lakh and pawned her jewellery worth about five lakh, the scamsters told her a property dealer would visit her home to help with the sale of property. Then, a person named Sushant Kumar visited her home, took her property papers and a sale agreement was signed with another person named Anil Kapoor posing as buyer and Praveen Chadha as witness.

World.title: DDA inks pact to develop 5-star hotel in Delhi’s Dwarka; opening set for 2030
World.content:
The Delhi Development Authority (DDA) has signed an agreement with Juniper Hotels Ltd. to develop a five-star hotel in Dwarka’s Sector 23. This is the first of four special licence-fee projects auctioned by the authority over the past year to reach the agreement stage.

The hotel, overlooking the Dwarka Golf Course, is expected to attract an investment of more than ₹1,000 crore and create around 800 direct jobs, as per a statement released by the DDA on Thursday. It is scheduled to become operational by 2030. Over its 55-year licence period, the project is projected to generate more than ₹6,000 crore in revenue for the DDA.

The agreement was signed on Wednesday between the DDA and Juniper Hospitality Assets Pvt. Ltd., a subsidiary of Juniper Hotels. The site is expected to be handed over to the company soon, the DDA said.

The hotel is proposed to be developed and operated under the Grand Hyatt brand through Juniper Hotels’ partnership with Hyatt. Juniper currently operates seven hotels with 1,895 rooms and serviced apartments across India, according to the DDA.

The project is part of the DDA’s wider effort to develop Dwarka as a commercial and investment hub under Lieutenant-Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu. The authority had auctioned four sites under a special licence-fee model, under which private developers build and operate projects on DDA land for a specified licence period.

The location is being positioned as a key advantage for the project, with the proposed hotel close to the Dwarka Golf Course, Yashobhoomi Convention Centre and Dwarka Sports Complex. It is also located opposite the proposed Diplomatic Enclave, which the DDA expects will add to demand for high-end accommodation in the area.

The agreement is the first formal licensing deal among those projects. The DDA expects the hotel to add to Dwarka’s hospitality infrastructure as the sub-city gains convention, sports and diplomatic facilities.

The agreement comes days after Mr. Sandhu held an interaction with industry representatives on accelerating Dwarka’s development as an economic and commercial centre.

World.title: Two children drown in rainwater-filled pit in Delhi’s Narela
World.content:
Two minor boys, aged nine and 11, drowned in a rainwater-filled pit in Delhi’s Narela area on Thursday, police said.

The children, both residents of Bawana, had entered the pit to play and swim near 100 Foota, close to the DDA Flats in Narela, when they drowned.

Following a distress call, the police rushed to the spot. The children were pulled out of the pit and taken to Satyawadi Raja Harish Chandra Hospital in Narela, where doctors declared them dead.

Their bodies were sent for medico-legal proceedings and legal action has been initiated, police said. The exact circumstances leading to the children entering the pit and the sequence of events preceding their drowning are being ascertained.

The incident occurred amid heavy monsoon activity in the national capital, with several parts of Delhi witnessing waterlogging and accumulation of rainwater.

Following the incident, the Delhi Development Authority (DDA) expressed regret over the deaths and said the incident took place on vacant land adjoining Housing Pocket-4 in Sector G7/G8, Narela.

The DDA said the vacant plot had been secured with a boundary wall to prevent unauthorised access, but portions of the wall had been repeatedly damaged despite repairs.

“Such incidents of damage, theft and unauthorised activities in the area have also been brought to the notice of the local police through complaints/FIRs and other communications from time to time,” the agency said.

The DDA said it had repeatedly taken up security and law-and-order concerns in Sector G7/G8 with the Delhi Police. It added that a flat in Pocket-4 had already been allotted for a police chowki, while two additional LIG flats had been offered for setting up a police camp office.

The agency said it was extending all necessary cooperation to the police and other authorities and was examining further preventive measures, including strengthening the boundary wall and enhancing surveillance of vulnerable vacant plots in the area.

Further investigation into the incident is under way.

World.title: Independence Day 2026: traffic snarls hit Delhi amid full-dress rehearsal restrictions; police on high alert
World.content:
Long queues of vehicles stretched across parts of Delhi on Thursday morning as traffic restrictions imposed for the Independence Day full-dress rehearsal at Red Fort collided with the city’s peak-hour rush, leaving commuters navigating diversions, blocked roads and snarls on key routes.

The Delhi-Dehradun highway saw a build-up of vehicles after the movement of heavy vehicles was restricted from 10 p.m. on Wednesday until 11 a.m. on Thursday. The restrictions, coupled with the morning rush, led to a backlog that took some time to clear even after heavy vehicles were allowed to move.

Across central Delhi, road closures and diversions around Red Fort added to the congestion, with commuters heading towards railway stations, schools and offices finding familiar routes blocked or redirected.

“Trying to reach Railway station and all directions are blocked due to Independence Day prep. If you travel today, more roads are blocked than announced. Put in extra time,” a commuter posted on X.

One of the key pressure points was the stretch around Shanti Van Chowk and Rajghat. Traffic police said some commuters travelling from the Salimgarh Bypass towards ITO continued to take the familiar route via Shanti Van despite advisories on the diversions, bringing them into restricted stretches and adding to the congestion.

“Despite the traffic restrictions announced in advance, commuters did not follow the diversions and ended up getting stuck on the restricted routes. Our personnel were guiding them to take alternative routes,” said DCP (Traffic), Central Range, Nishant Gupta.

Another pressure point emerged beneath the IP Flyover and around the Hanuman Mandir stretch. Vehicles were being diverted towards Mori Gate, but some motorists attempted to use Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Marg towards Old Delhi Railway Station, creating another chokepoint.

Mr. Gupta added that the congestion on the Delhi-Dehradun highway was linked to the restriction on heavy vehicle movement. Once the restrictions were lifted, traffic continued to move slowly for some time as the accumulated backlog was cleared.

The traffic disruptions came as Delhi Police and other security agencies stepped up preparations for the 80th Independence Day celebrations at Red Fort. A full-dress rehearsal was held at the historic venue on Thursday to test security, traffic management and the movement of personnel ahead of the main ceremony on August 15.

The rehearsal offered residents in central Delhi a preview of the main ceremony, with helicopters showering the venue with tri colours as students assembled at the Red Fort in arrangements similar to those planned for Independence Day.

“The entire police force is on high alert. We conducted a full-dress rehearsal today, in which we identified areas for improvement and will further strengthen the arrangements based on those observations,” said Special Commissioner of Police (Law and Order) Devesh Chandra Srivastava.

Security has been intensified around Red Fort and across several parts of central Delhi, with police personnel carrying out foot patrols, checking hotels and homestays, conducting mock drills and identifying habitual offenders. Bike Tiranga rallies have also been held as part of the preparations.

In north-east Delhi, around 200 police personnel, including officers and station house officers, participated in a mock drill focused on crowd control and responses to agitations, demonstrations and riot-like situations.

Personnel underwent practical training in the deployment of water cannons, Vajra vehicles, tear-smoke guns and other anti-riot equipment. The drill focused on coordination, quick response, formation and tactical positioning to deal with large gatherings and potential law-and-order challenges.

Meanwhile, security measures have also been strengthened at Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International Airport ahead of Independence Day. The Central Industrial Security Force has increased deployment, while random checks, thorough frisking and dummy security checks are being conducted as part of covert security audits.

During such checks, undercover personnel attempt to bypass security checkpoints with simulated prohibited items to test the alertness, response times and screening procedures of personnel on duty. Dog squads and Quick Response Teams have also been deployed, with operational drills continuing at the airport.

The airport has advised passengers to reach early as enhanced security screening could take longer than usual.

World.title: Punjab Assembly polls: BJP’s pro-Sikh strategy gives AAP scope for Hindu outreach
World.content:
Ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly election, political parties in the State are getting their houses in order.

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), a party traditionally associated with Hindu voters, is working to project itself as pro-Sikh, even as the Congress, the principal Opposition, continues to grapple with infighting. The ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) is focused on consolidating the Hindu vote, a voter base it shares with the BJP and the Congress, as it seeks to retain power.

The BJP recently appointed Kewal Singh Dhillon, a Jat Sikh face, as its Punjab president. Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini, often seen donning a dastar (turban), has been making frequent visits to Punjab for social and religious functions.
